When you’re drawing background shrubs and plants, the silhouette can do most of the work.

Instead of trying to draw every leaf, start by designing one larger interesting shape.

Push parts outward. Cut areas back in. Create overlaps, gaps, uneven heights, and changes in direction. Avoid repeating the same shapes over and over.

Once the silhouette feels natural, add just enough internal texture to suggest leaves, branches, and smaller plants.

This is a great way to simplify complicated backgrounds without making them feel empty or overworked.

Think about the big shape first. Let the details support it.', 'datetime': '2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4020909579943688805', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-sjc6-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/885491780_18493756573106513_6453903156205692147_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=109&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiQ0xJUFMuYmVzdF9pbWFnZV91cmxnZW4uQzMifQ%3D%3D&_nc_ohc=3XjFWOBUDtYQ7kNvwHKfDu3&_nc_oc=AdqxeazKS5Mby3BqzAkPeZP90l5EuHz556OsmlsEeBdVUQ6kQNunXWD5vhV7RjDtc0w&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-sjc6-1.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=17qNuxBKpJmR6qbMw3o8qA&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQSkUGPYgpog0t1OmZ8paBHeOx2ugEZY6mVLRQ8aAc8hHA&oe=6AED47A7', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Video', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/DfNI_WSgjpl'}, {'caption': 'Comment DRILLS and I’ll DM you the info for the Drawing Drills course.

A ram’s horn is a perfect subject for practicing cross-contour hatching because the form is constantly curving, twisting, and changing direction in space.

Instead of using hatch marks just to make areas darker, wrap them around the horn like bands around a tube.

As the horn bends toward or away from you, the direction and curvature of those lines change with it.

Now your hatching is doing more than creating value. It’s showing the viewer how the surface turns, which direction it faces, and how the entire horn moves through 3D space.

When you’re learning how to draw, make every line communicate something.

Shade the form while you describe the form.', 'datetime': '2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4020903238197854872', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-sjc3-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/885294845_18493753903106513_1937268322796053416_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=105&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiQ0xJUFMuYmVzdF9pbWFnZV91cmxnZW4uQzMifQ%3D%3D&_nc_ohc=PaW720BLe7gQ7kNvwGZ7bzC&_nc_oc=Adrgu3TZ7xWiQja450fO5OydhVSR03KcUM5g7rcg9X54Uj3ukA8sGVWTN-rTZO1WSUQ&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-sjc3-1.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=17qNuxBKpJmR6qbMw3o8qA&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQR1DkusoHuVMkd-I-J9JvNb09nnLP_1X-K5J4zFWkEs5w&oe=6AED3706', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Video', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/DfNHjEFAEKY'}, {'caption': 'Comment DRILLS and I’ll DM you the info for the Drawing Drills course.

If you want to learn how to draw lily pads, start with one of the simplest shapes you already know: an ellipse.

Draw an ellipse in perspective, then cut a small slit from the edge toward the center. Think of it almost like a flattened Pac-Man shape.

That simple modification immediately starts turning a basic geometric shape into something recognizable.

Change the width and angle of your ellipses as the lily pads tilt and turn across the water. Overlap them, vary their size, and then add the veins, shadows, and smaller details.

This is one of the core ideas behind Drawing Drills: complicated subjects become much easier when you learn to see the simple shapes underneath them.

One drawing made with masking fluid. 

Freddy Krueger. Jason Voorhees. Chucky. Pennywise. Frankenstein’s monster. Michael Myers.

For the creamy chicken filling :

2 tbsp butter 
1/2 cup yellow onion, finely chopped 
1 tbsp fresh garlic, minced 
2 cup rotisserie chicken , shredded 
Salt to taste
1 tsp garlic powder 
1/2 tsp black pepper powder 
1 tsp paprika powder 
1 tsp red chili flakes
1/4 cup unsweetened heavy whipping cream 
5 tbsp cream cheese 
1/4 cup green onion, chopped 
1/4 cup Parmesan cheese , freshly grated 
1 tbsp parsley, chopped 

To assemble 
6 sliced bread of choice 
1 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese, shredded 
Butter for toasting 

Method:
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the shredded rotisserie chicken, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and chili flakes. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes so the seasonings coat the chicken.

as a first-generation south asian american, staying connected to my roots hasn’t always been easy!

america doesn’t really make space for different cultural and religious celebrations. with no guaranteed time off for hindu holidays and the hustle of everyday american life, celebrating the way we would in india can feel almost impossible.

additionally, my parents moved to wherever their business had the best opportunities, which meant growing up pretty isolated from the gujarati community. outside of dance class, i didn’t have indians friends—there were only two others at my school. between their own hustle, my parents did everything they could to teach us about our culture, religion, and the traditions that connected us to our roots.

today, if you ask any gujarati american about their favorite time of year, chances are they’ll say navratri ❤️‍🔥

growing up, it was my chance to pull out all the gorgeous indian outfits i didnt get to wear otherwise, put together my favorite bangle combinations, and wear those statement earrings that looked SO good but hurt by the end of the night 💃🏻

weekend after weekend, we’d drive to nearby towns, dress up in new outfits, eat our favorite indian street food, and dance all night (garba). people of all ages and backgrounds came together to dance, pray, and celebrate the divine feminine 💫

navratri is so much more than the outfits, food, and garba. it’s a celebration of the triumph of the divine feminine energy and maa durga’s victory over evil. in India, the celebration lasts nine nights to honor her nine forms, each representing different qualities of the divine feminine: power, courage, wisdom, compassion, protection, strength, devotion, destruction, and transformation. 

for me, growing up gujarati american, navratri was more than a festival. it was a way to reconnect with my roots, find my community, and feel closer to a part of myself that wasn’t part of my everyday life 🪷

However, I woke up feeling energized and very confident attempting another big peak day. So onwards to Black Peak’s NE Ridge. How was it? GNARLY. Way spicier than I was expecting and probably my new favorite ridge scramble. The easiest comparison in Colorado (that I’ve done) I think would be Little Bear’s West Ridge-Direct route but this was even spicier. Insane exposure and multiple moves in the low 5th class range. Felt like adrenaline was flooding my veins the entire ridge until I reached the summit. Comment “Recipe” and I’ll send you the full recipe for free.

This is the easiest way to make crunchwraps at home. It feeds a whole family, costs way less than takeout, and tastes even better.

If you’re always looking for new dinner ideas, you’re in the right place. That’s why I share simple and affordable meals that save you time and money.

Follow for more weeknight staples.

Ingredients

Crunchwrap
• 8 burrito-size tortillas
• 2 lb ground beef
• 1 cup beef broth
• 6 tbsp taco seasoning (or homemade: 3 tbsp chili powder, 3 tbsp cumin, 2 tbsp garlic powder, 2 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp oregano, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tbsp black pepper)
• 1½ cups shredded cheddar cheese
• 6 tostadas
• 2 cups shredded lettuce
• 2 tomatoes, diced
• 1 cup sour cream
• 3 tbsp butter, melted

Creamy Taco Sauce
• ⅓ cup sour cream or Greek yogurt
• ⅓ cup mayonnaise
• ⅓ cup milk or water
• Juice of 1 lime
• 1 tbsp taco seasoning
• 1 tbsp dried parsley
• ½ tsp paprika
• ½ tsp garlic powder

Instructions
1.	Lay the tortillas around the edges of a sheet pan so the centers sit on the lip of the pan, then place one tortilla flat in the middle. Spread about ¾ cup sour cream across the tortillas.
2.	In a skillet, cook the ground beef with taco seasoning and beef broth until browned and the liquid is absorbed. Optional: For extra flavor, add 1 diced onion and 6 cloves of minced garlic.
3.	Add the beef over the sour cream, then layer shredded cheese, tostadas, shredded lettuce, and diced tomatoes.
4.	Add a tortilla with the remaining 1/4 cup sour cream in the middle. Fold the tortillas over the top to fully enclose everything, then brush with melted butter.
5.	Top with another baking sheet and bake at 420°F for 20 minutes. Remove the top sheet and bake for another 7 minutes until golden and crispy.

Sauce
1.	Add all ingredients to a bowl.
2.	Whisk until smooth and fully combined.
3.	Let sit for 15–30 minutes in the fridge if you have time.

I kept hearing this dumpling bake was one of the easiest dinners of all time, and it lives up to it. Everything goes into one pan, straight into the oven, and dinner’s done with almost no effort. It’s quick, affordable, and perfect for busy weeknights when you still want something really good.

If you’re tired of eating the same boring meals every week, this is exactly why I share Weeknight Staples.

Follow me to eat better and spend less.

Ingredients
•	1 can full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz)
•	2 tbsp red curry paste
•	3 garlic cloves, minced
•	2 tsp fresh ginger, minced
•	3 tbsp soy sauce
•	1 tbsp oyster sauce
•	1 tbsp peanut butter
•	1 tbsp sesame oil
•	2 tsp rice vinegar

Instructions
1.	Preheat oven to 400°F.

3.	Squeeze in the lime juice.
4.	Stir in the chopped bok choy.
5.	Arrange the frozen dumplings on top in a single layer.

7.	Finish with chili crisp, green onions, sesame seeds, lime and cilantro if desired. Serve hot.

This is one of my favorite takeout meals. It’s gotten so expensive lately, so I started making it at home for a fraction of the cost. The flavor is even better and it makes plenty for the whole family.

Chicken Shawarma
• 2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs
• 3 tbsp olive oil
• 2 tbsp tomato paste
• ⅓ cup Greek yogurt
• Juice of 1 lemon

• 2 tsp cumin

1.	Slice chicken thighs into thin strips and add to a large bowl.

4.	Cut the tops off two garlic heads, drizzle with olive oil and salt, wrap in foil, and place in a baking dish with the chicken.
5.	Bake at 425°F for 25 minutes until the chicken is golden and slightly charred.
6.	Squeeze the roasted garlic into the chicken and toss before serving.

One of my favorite ways to cook Thanksgiving turkey. No overnight prep, just three ingredients for crispy skin and incredibly juicy meat. Plus, spatchcocking cuts down the cooking time so you’re not spending all day in the kitchen.

Here’s how I make it on my @traegergrills 

Ingredients
• 1 whole turkey (12–14 lb), fully thawed
• Salted butter (whole sticks and melted for injecting)
• Olive oil
• Your favorite BBQ rub

Instructions
1. Spatchcock: Place the turkey breast-side down and cut along both sides of the backbone with poultry shears. Remove it, flip the turkey over, tuck the wings underneath, and turn the legs outward. Press down until the breastbone cracks and the turkey lies flat. This helps the legs cook thoroughly without overcooking the breasts, keeping the meat juicy.

Dumpling Filling

• 1 tsp black pepper
• 2 tbsp chili crisp
• 3 tbsp soy sauce
• 1½ tsp sesame oil
• 1 tbsp rice vinegar

• Soy sauce

3. Heat avocado oil in a pan over medium heat. Arrange the dumplings wrapper-side down, then lightly drizzle a little more avocado oil over the top. Cook for 2–3 minutes, or until the bottoms begin to lightly brown.
4. Pour in the chicken broth, cover with a lid, and steam for 7 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for another 2 minutes.

recipe:

pumpkin loaf:
½ cup granulated sugar (100g)
½ cup packed brown sugar (100g)
½ cup neutral oil (110g)
2 large eggs, room temp
1 cup pumpkin purée (180g)
1 tsp vanilla extract
¼ cup milk, room temp (60g)
2 cups all-purpose flour (240g)
1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp baking soda
½ tsp salt
1 tsp pumpkin pie spice

cinnamon filling:
¼ cup softened butter (57g)
½ cup packed brown sugar (100g)
2 tbsp cinnamon
1 tbsp all-purpose flour (8g)

cream cheese frosting:
4 oz cream cheese, room temp (113g)
2 tbsp butter, room temp (28g)
powdered sugar, to taste
1 tsp vanilla paste
cinnamon, for topping

instructions:
mix the sugars with the eggs until the mixture is slightly pale and fluffy, add in the oil, pumpkin purée, vanilla, and milk. sift in the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice and fold until just combined.

mix the cinnamon filling ingredients until combined. the butter should be softened, not melted, so the filling holds its shape instead of turning into a puddle.

spread a thin layer of pumpkin batter into a lined loaf pan. alternate dollops of pumpkin batter with the cinnamon filling, then add another layer of pumpkin batter and continue alternating until everything is used, finishing with pumpkin batter.

bake at 375°f for 5 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°f and bake for about 50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the loaf comes out without wet batter. check a few spots since the cinnamon layers can make testing a little tricky. let the loaf cool before frosting.

beat the cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla paste until smooth. spread over the cooled loaf and sprinkle with cinnamon. enjoyyyy!

[{'caption': '“What if instead of “us vs. them” we saw ALL of us vs. extremism…”

And worked together to BUILD a future where we acknowledge each other’s humanity and find solutions to our most challenging problems?

Recognizing the global interconnectivity of extremist thinking, and the worldwide challenges posed by toxic polarization, Starts With Us is building upon our foundational work to take our mission global with Builders — a non-profit focused on overcoming toxic polarization worldwide, and on solving our most challenging problems.

We’re still doing what we have always done — equipping people with the skills, tools, and networks to overcome toxic polarization and find solutions together but under a new global initiative that opens the discussion to issues beyond our borders.

What is a Builder?

Builders are flexible thinkers and constructive problem solvers who recognize the dignity of all people. We:
1. Reject violent absolutism and dehumanization
2. Balance passionate convictions with critical thinking
3. Take action to solve problems together

Are you ready to be a Builder?

💥 This 4 ingredient appetizer comes together so quickly yet it packs all the fall flavors in every bite! The simple ingredients make it so easy to whip together for a potluck, family or friend gathering or all the holidays heading our way! 
.
🎃I wait all year for that pumpkin butter to come in stock and it has finally hit the shelves! 
.
🛍️Grab 
- 1 jar pumpkin butter 
- 1 bag toasted, unsalted pecan pieces 
- 2 boxes fig and olive crackers 
- 1 large slice triple cream Brie 
.
🔥I love using my cast iron skillet for this recipe. It makes it really easy to throw all the ingredients in and it helps keep everything warm as this dish is enjoyed. 
.
♨️Preheat oven to 350. 
.
📝Start by placing the Brie in the skillet. Then pour the pumpkin butter over the top. In a separate sheet pan pour the pecans on. I get the unsalted, toasted pecan pieces but love to toast them a bit more to get that fragrant toasted pecan. Place both items in the oven and bake until the Brie is bubbling and melting and you can smell the toasted nuts. Sprinkle the pecans over the Brie and pumpkin butter. 
I like to put my crackers outside the cast iron to keep them crisp and easy to grab. 
Using a cheese knife or spoon scoop this gooey, creamy, deliciousness onto your crackers and enjoy! 
.
🙌🏻 Honestly, this is an addicting appetizer and you best stock up on the ingredients before they are gone! 
.

Aren’t you tired, I ask my heart?
Haven’t you had enough to endure?
Why be miserable when you can learn to ignore?
Every time I see her, you create these ripples that shake my core.
Why this urge to know every bit of her more?
Why don’t you choose a story that I can afford?

The heart replied:
oh boy,
I have tried to rescue myself from you,
But you cheat on me more than I can cheat on you,
for you care for her just as much as I care for you.
Fair enough, I said.
Then I ask of you again,
to let her go,
to let my mind breathe out of
her touch,
to dry her out of my
thoughts forever,
to let my eyes, swim another
way,
to let her memory be a lie,
let this not be a story where I
even try.
Remember, there is no need for her to know.
Don’t you see it,
we are perfect as long as our hearts aren’t exposed.
Can we please just open another champagne and cry,
I can write it as a story,
daydream it as a nightmare,
sell it as a fiction,
narrate it like a poem,
edit it like a thief, taking away the words that mean the most,
and she will never know half of it.
Would you support me then?
The heart replies:
I am tired of your lies,
you are as much a tragedy to me as I am to you,
because you bleed for this story more than I bleed for you.
You ask me to change,
but as soon as I attempt to try, you hold me a mirror,
to remind,
That you are me as much as I am you.

One day, I cried like the heavens plead when their lords die.
I felt as if I were left alone in the middle of the sky,
where even my loneliness felt lonely,
where I lived reality like a nightmare,
as I suffered from suffering that were never mine.
But suddenly something caught my eye;
I saw an old lady passing by,
her shoulders shrugged with age;
she was experiencing excruciating pain
as medical tubes threaded in and out of her body.
Yet sitting in her wheelchair,
she kept offering smiles.
She had lost more than I could write,
yet her smile was shinier than the stars
that shone among the darkest skies.
There was depth in her smile and genuine love in the way she cared;
the worst of life couldn’t break her into fear,
even though she was made of the same skin and bones as I...
Finally, with courage, I asked—what gave her the strength,
even when she looked at others living normal lives?
Pushing her trembling hand past her tubes,
she pressed it on my chest
and said, “For as long as this beats for you,
remember, you have the ability to try.
For one day, we will all die,
and whatever little you create
is still more than what you had when you first cried.
And don’t worry about me,
there is some tranquility even in despair,
but first, you have to acknowledge that you need care;
only then can you heal and become a guide for others
through their despair.”
The silence of the moment caught me by, I shed a tear that was never mine.
Looking at her, I aged in my mind.
Since then, my life has been a reverberation of her replies;
no amount of adversity can tremble my faith,
and at every trial I face, I tell life,
that my love for you will never die
even if I had to suffer from
sufferings that were
never meant to be
mine.

they say—find your perspective.

From colonial streets and Gothic cathedrals to Art Deco masterpieces and futuristic skyscrapers, NYC is a place where the old and the new stand side by side 🏛️

You’ll find some of the city’s oldest architecture in areas like Lower Manhattan, the Financial District, Greenwich Village and parts of Brooklyn. Meanwhile Midtown and Hudson Yards are home to some of NYC’s most ambitious modern skyscrapers 🏗️

And the best part? New York never stops growing. The skyline keeps changing, new buildings continue to rise and every generation leaves its mark on the city 🗽

So let’s take a look at 5 architectural landmarks from my video 👇

1️⃣ Chrysler Building 🏙️
Completed in 1930 and designed by William Van Alen, this Art Deco icon was built for Walter P. Chrysler and is famous for its stunning stainless-steel crown

📍 405 Lexington Avenue, at East 42nd Street

2️⃣ Louis Vuitton Fifth Avenue 👜🏗️
Located inside a landmark Art Deco building, Louis Vuitton’s temporary Fifth Avenue home is a beautiful example of historic architecture meeting modern New York

📍 6 East 57th Street, between Fifth and Madison Avenues

3️⃣ Cartier Fifth Avenue 💎🏛️
Located inside the historic Cartier Mansion, this elegant Fifth Avenue landmark was once a private residence and is one of the most beautiful architectural gems on the avenue

📍 653 Fifth Avenue, at East 52nd Street

4️⃣ Empire State Building 🏙️✨
Completed in 1931, this iconic Art Deco skyscraper was designed by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and remains one of the most famous symbols of New York City

📍 350 Fifth Avenue, at West 34th Street

5️⃣ Radio City Music Hall 🎭✨
Opened in 1932, this iconic Art Deco theater is famous for its spectacular interior and has been one of New York’s most beloved entertainment venues for decades

📍 1260 Avenue of the Americas, at West 50th Street

✅Which of these landmarks is your favorite? ❤️ Save this for your next NYC architecture walk and share it with someone who loves New York! 🗽🏙️

📅 2004–2016 | 👤 Santiago Calatrava

📍 768 5th Ave

What began as a dream to help just one child has grown into a movement that now supports 220 children every single day with meals, education, clothing, medical care, and hope.

Every smile you see, every meal served, every child in school, and every life changed is possible because of people around the world who chose to care.

This is more than a charity. It’s a family. It’s a promise that no child should be forgotten simply because they were born into poverty.

I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who has walked this journey with us over the past seven years. But our mission is far from over. There are still many children waiting for hope.

If our story touches your heart, I invite you to become part of this mission. You can volunteer, donate, sponsor a child, or simply share our work with others. Every act of kindness changes a life.

❤️ Together, we can build a future where every child has the opportunity to dream, learn, and thrive.

unlike most, my idea of good weather rhymes with rain, fog, and gray. that’s when i put on a trench coat, grab my camera, and wander toward the gloomiest forest or the coziest café. there’s something so aesthetic in the blur, muted tones, nostalgia tucked into shadows, everything feeling just right.

i still remember one november afternoon in 2019, stepping out of the spring street subway into drizzle, new yorkers rushing past, umbrellas colliding, headlights shimmering in puddles. it felt heavy and cinematic, my first time seeing the city soaked. a year later, i would call manhattan home, and since then, rainy days here have become my muse. now i chase this weather everywhere, cities, beaches, mountains, islands, always refreshing my weather app, always looking for clouds.

and that’s what brings me here: these presets. for a long time, i hesitated to share them. my edits are subtle, because the real secret is the weather itself. but there are small details i amplify, tones, contrasts, little adjustments that shape the mood. i’ve gathered them so you can bring a touch of that same atmosphere into your own work. simple, moody, yours to play with, the presets are available through the link in my bio 💌

1 snow flakes = 6 paper doily’s 
For each doily you should:
1. Fold the doily into 4ths and then open the doily flat
2. Fold in two opposite sides to the center 
3.  Put a piece of paper under the folded in parts and add a small amount of glue to both sides, making sure not to get the glue on the doily under the folds (hence, the paper you placed under them) 
4. Remove the paper. Then fold the doily in half, like a hamburger. Make sure the parts you added glue to are the only parts that are sticking together.
5. Repeat these steps on all 6 doilys.
6. Then, add glue to the outside portions of the folded doilies and stick all them all together
7. Eventually you can add glue to the outside of the final doily and bring the first doily around and stick them together. It should look like a snowflake!

A witness to the deadly shooting inside a Halloween store at a Bay Area mall described the terrifying scene as shots rang out and she ducked for cover — fearing she was “going to die” as several victims were struck by gunfire.

Jocelyn Lopez Tabares, 15, and her 23-year-old sister were picking up last-minute accessories for their costumes Friday night at the Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield when a barrage of shots erupted.

“I felt like I was going to die,” Lopez Tabares, of Vallejo, told the California Post. “I thought it was going to be my last time living. I didn’t want to die that way.”

The shooting, which left one person dead and six others injured, was a “targeted incident” carried out by a lone gunman, police announced. The suspect remained on the run as of Saturday afternoon.

Lopez Tabares, who was standing near the checkout registers, initially mistook the gunfire for popping balloons, until her sister dragged her to the concrete floor, she recalled

“We were in line getting ready to leave,” Lopez Tabares said. “Out of nowhere, we just hear at least 10 shots go off. I thought it was a balloon popping. I was in shock, and everyone just went down. My sister pulled me down because I couldn’t move. I was so scared.”

As dozens of shoppers scrambled toward the exits in panic, the 15-year-old found herself frozen on the floor.

The teen then pulled out her cellphone and began recording, determined to document the scene in case she did not survive.

Here’s a guy who’s been out there, getting his hands dirty with the rest of us and actually giving a crap about the people who keep this country running. Plumbers, sparkies, masons, farmers - you name it. He’s worked with ‘em and shown the world what we’re really about.

As a Coast Guard veteran and someone who spent 10 years as a diesel mechanic, I now host a podcast called Bucket Talk where we highlight folks in the trades and construction. I also work at BRUNT, where we make gear that can actually hold up to what we put it through. So meeting a guy like Mike, who’s spent his whole career shouting from the rooftops about how important this work is? That hits home.

Mike’s always saying how we’ve lost sight of how critical the trades are, and he’s spot on. I see it all the time - people acting like this work is a fallback instead of a damn good career. But the reality is, we’re the ones keeping the lights on and the water flowing.

Talking with Mike reminded me why I’m so passionate about what I do at BRUNT - whether it’s telling stories on the podcast or supporting the people out there grinding every day in those “dirty jobs”. There’s dignity and pride (and money) in this work, and we gotta make sure the next generation knows it too.

That’s a big reason why BRUNT was created: to build a brand that actually cares about the people who rely on their gear. A lot of these other big workwear brands lost sight of the people they originally built their gear for and have instead chased trends, fashion, or whatever could get them more profit. BRUNT isn’t into all of that. We’re about making high-quality gear by listening to what our customers actually need and want in the field, always remembering that we’re nothing without them.

So here’s to all the men and women getting dirty in the trades, doing what needs to get done - and to Mike Rowe, for making sure people see us for what we really are: the backbone of this country.

There was a time when a new baby meant meals on the porch. Surgery meant someone checked on your family. A death meant neighbors gathered. An accident meant people came together.

Not because anyone was incapable of handling life.

But because that’s what community did.

Somewhere along the way, we’ve become so focused on independence, convenience, and not inconveniencing others that we’ve lost something meaningful.

And it’s not just happening in churches. It’s happening in our neighborhoods, friendships, and families.

People are quietly struggling while surrounded by people who would probably help if they knew.

Sometimes by the time we notice, the hurt runs deep.

I’m not suggesting we abandon boundaries or show up uninvited. I’m suggesting we normalize thoughtful, practical care again.

Bring the meal. Check on the neighbor. Remember the grieving family after the funeral. Offer to pick up groceries. Make room for people to receive kindness without feeling like a burden.

We weren’t meant to do every season of life alone.

Stare into a mirror in a dim room, and within a minute your face starts becoming someone else.

In 2010, psychologist Giovanni Caputo put the Bloody Mary dare to the test: fifty adults stared at their own reflection in a dim room for ten minutes. Two thirds saw their face deform, more than a quarter saw a stranger, almost half saw a monster, and a few saw a parent who had died. None of it was in the glass. The likely culprit is how your visual system handles a face that never changes; the exact mechanism is still debated.

Your thumb does the exact same thing every time you click a pen, so how does the pen know whether to push the tip out or pull it back in?

Inside the barrel sits a tiny plastic crown on top of the spring-loaded ink. Slanted teeth on the button turn each straight push into a small twist, so the crown steps round one notch at a time, always the same way. Its lugs land on ridges inside the barrel that alternate: a short stop that holds the ink down with the tip out, then a deep slot that lets the spring push everything up with the tip in. The pen is counting to two.

Simplified 3D model: designs differ between pens in the number of ridges and the size of each step, and some click pens use a different latch.

[{'caption': "I was 24 the last time I introduced myself on here which feels like lifetimes ago because, well, it was. 

I'm still moving and shaking and flowing and growing but now as a single mom of two cats on the brink of 26. 

When I worked in PR (which, again, feels like lifetimes ago and since that run began just a year post-pandemic, it kind of was) I was often told to cut shit short. No bullshit. No flour. No one has time. 

While the old soul author in me feels otherwise, the Libra in me sees value. 

This is Jada (J for short), in short.

I'm a former (though I prefer the term forever) dancer, current yogi and self-proclaimed mat rat – a term I'm reclaiming for those just really into mat-based movement. I'm a Jersey girl with west-coast whimsy and often tinker with a cross-country move. 

I know movement as a gift. When I say this, I think of my late mother, my grandmother on hospice, myself when I've caught a cold and spend the sickness wishing for health. Acknowledge your gift, open it, exercise it, say thank you and thank you and thank you for it. 

Did I tell you I'm Libra? I flirt with life like a butterfly to a flower. Curiosity keeps me connected. Life is as exciting as the number of times you're willing to say yes. 

On that note, I love life. Wholly, deeply, truly. I fancy Thursdays, the way the morning sun dances in my kitchen, how September feels like January 1st and the way dogs tilt their heads and people almost always follow suit. 

& on that one, I rack up miles for how frequently I pay the state of gratitude a visit. Today and often for the now 100K+ bunch of movers, shakers, friends – t h a n k  y o u for being here 🥲 what else do you want to see or hear or know? 💭

My name is Hunter. I’m an outdoor creator & commercial photographer/videographer currently based in Humboldt County. I grew up in this area all my life until 23. It was here where I found my love for photography. I would go out exploring the redwoods and coastal beaches around me, but then I was feeling stuck so I decided to make the 32+ hour drive over to Nashville to try to get into the concert photography scene. This was peak covid so that ended up not happening. During that time I would go out to various places in and out of Nashville exploring what the area has to offer. After a couple years of living out there and realizing it wasn’t where I wanted to fully settle down at, I decided to make the move to Las Vegas ! VEGAS BABY! 

Here is where I would go explore the desert and see what the Southwest has to offer. Now one misconception about Vegas is that it’s all gambling and alcohol, while yes that’s true, there’s sooo much more to the amazing city. The people, the hospitality, the neighborhoods all made it feel like it was a small town. As long as you were off strip and Fremont it truly feels like a community there believe it or not. During that time I continued freelancing and visiting places such as Valley of Fire (a lot) and Death Valley it made me fall in love with the desert. 

Fast forward 2 years, I moved back to my hometown, but I knew it wasn’t where I wanted to truly be. So I decided to build a bed in the back of my car and travel the desert some more. I spent the next 2 months at the end of 2024 traveling back through the desert and roaming all over Utah, Arizona, Nevada, and Southern California exploring new places, meeting new friends, and figuring out who I am and what I want in life. 

Now that I’m back in my hometown again with my best friend, Maverick. I’m craving that sense of adventure, and that will be changing very soon. Being stagnant is not for me. Ask anyone that knows me! They’ll tell you the same thing.

For the dough

* 200 g warm milk
* 200 g warm water
* 115 g vegetable oil
* 30 g egg white
* 10 g instant yeast
* 8 g sugar
* 12 g salt
* 560–600 g all-purpose flour
* 12 g matcha powder

For the filling

* Nutella and or chocolate pieces, as needed

For the top

* 1 egg yolk, about 18 g

Instructions

Start with the warm milk, warm water, vegetable oil, egg white, yeast, sugar, and salt. Mix everything together, then gradually add the flour and knead until you have a nice, soft dough. You don’t want the dough too dry, so add the last part of the flour slowly.

Divide the dough into two equal pieces. Keep one dough plain. Add the matcha powder to the other half and knead until the matcha is completely incorporated and the dough has an even green color.

Cover both doughs and let them rise for about 40 minutes.

Roll out the plain dough. Place the matcha dough in the center, then fold the plain dough around it and seal it. Roll everything out together into a large circle.

Cut the dough into triangles. Add your chocolate spread or chocolate pieces to the wide end of each triangle, then roll them up into croissant shapes.

Place them on a baking tray, cover, and let them proof for another 30 minutes.

[{'caption': 'After lots of prayer and fasting over the past two weeks, I’m super excited to announce my commitment to play soccer at Texas Tech University! ❤️🖤

I’m so grateful for my faith and my Savior Jesus Christ. He has guided and directed every step of my journey, even when things were hard or I didn’t know which direction to take. He has shown me—over and over—that “all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.” I’ve felt His hand leading me, shaping me, and preparing me for this opportunity.

Lubbock already feels like home. I was blown away by the amazing campus and the Texas Tech pride that fills the city. I can’t wait to give everything I have to this place and work every single day to make y’all proud.

I’m also so grateful for everyone at BYU who supported me and helped me grow into the player and person I am today. Your love means the world. 

To the Texas Tech staff — thank you for believing in me and giving me the chance to write this new chapter. I won’t take a single day for granted.

I’m fired up, grateful, and ready to get to work. God opened this door, and I’m walking through it with faith and everything I’ve got.

Understanding these thresholds (and this graph) can help you train at the right intensity for your goals, rather than just guessing based on pace or heart rate!

2 things to note that wasn’t included in the video:

1️⃣ Heart rate here is a proxy for exercise intensity.

It’s useful for estimating how hard you’re working, but it doesn’t directly relate lactate. 

Factors like heat, fatigue and hydration can also affect it.

2️⃣ Everyone’s graph will look slightly different 

Your thresholds and the heart rates they occur at won’t necessarily be the same as this graph, but the principals remain the same!

To summarise the key points: 

• LT1 (Aerobic Threshold) 

This is the point where blood lactate starts to rise consistently above baseline. It helps identify the upper end of easier aerobic training.

• LT2 (Anaerobic Threshold) 

This is the point where blood lactate starts rising much more rapidly. This is particularly important for understanding threshold training and how hard you can sustain an effort.

Why does this matter? 

Your thresholds help guide your training intensities, whether you’re preparing for a 10km, Half Marathon or Ironman…

The goal isn’t just to train harder, it’s to understand WHAT you’re trying to improve and WHY you’re training at a particular intensities, which will improve your specific efficiencies based on your desired outcome 💪🏻

A season of growing, giving, and sustaining life while watching yourself grow, too. Of feeling an overwhelming sense of love alongside exhaustion, uncertainty, and moments when you hardly recognize the person staring back at you in the mirror. Of learning to give so much of yourself while remembering that you deserve care, too.

The highs are incredible, but the hard days are real. And somewhere between the sleepless nights, changing bodies, shifting identities, and little moments that make it all worth it, we find a new version of ourselves.

Here’s to holding space for the whole experience—the joy, the struggle, the healing, and everything in between. We were never meant to do this alone. 🤍✨

To every mama in the thick of it: I see you. We see each other. And we’re in this together. 🫶🏼

You may be wondering, “What exactly is an APP?” An Advanced Practice Provider (APP) is a highly trained healthcare professional who provides comprehensive care and works with you to address your health concerns, answer your questions, and help you stay healthy.

APPs include Nurse Practitioners (NPs) and Physician Assistants (PAs). Depending on their training, specialty, and state regulations, APPs can:

* Evaluate your symptoms and medical concerns
* Diagnose and treat many health conditions
* Order and interpret laboratory tests and imaging
* Prescribe medications
* Provide preventive care and health education
* Help manage chronic conditions
* Refer you to specialists when needed

APPs may work independently or as part of a healthcare team, collaborating with physicians and other healthcare professionals when appropriate.

Most importantly, your visit is about you. Your APP is here to listen, answer your questions, provide evidence-based care, and partner with you in reaching your health goals. 🤍

“I am here for you.”

It’s a simple sentence, but I’ve watched what happens when people hear it.

A sigh of relief.
Tense shoulders begin to relax.
A worried expression softens.
Sometimes, a smile that seems to say, “Finally. Someone is listening.”

Over the years, patients have asked me, “Why aren’t more healthcare providers like you?”

The truth is, there are so many incredible people in healthcare who care deeply about their patients while working within a system that can leave them stretched thin and burned out.

Maybe my nursing training gives me a different perspective on connecting with patients. Maybe it’s simply who I am. I genuinely love what I do, and I genuinely care about the people who trust me with their health.

I’ve always tried to care for the person sitting in front of me the way I would want someone to care for my own family—with compassion, curiosity, honesty, and respect.

And that is what I want to bring here. On this page, I’ll share what I know, what I’m still learning, the lessons medicine has taught me, the practical tips I use every day, and pieces of the life behind the white coat.

Thank you for being here and supporting this new chapter. Follow along, share what resonates, and send it to someone who might need it too.

I am here for you.
I am here for us. 🤍

— Lisy M. Alvarez, APRN, FNP-BC, DipACLM

DORIAN GRAY — THE YEARS I NEVER WORE

I. THE WISH
I begged the years to leave my face alone,
to carve their hunger into paint, not bone.
Let every kiss remain my first.
Let beauty never learn to thirst.
I called it freedom. What a lovely lie:
to keep the face and let the person die.

II. THE FRAME
Behind me hangs the man I will not meet,
while velvet makes my cowardice look sweet.
Each kindness I refused, each heart I broke,
returns in brushstrokes where I never spoke.
Look at me.
No, not there.
Please—not yet.
The thing inside the frame has learned to stare.

III. THE APPLAUSE
They loved my mouth. They never asked its cost.
They praised my youth. I counted what it lost.
The silver shone. The candles ate the room.
I wore a perfect collar to my private tomb.
How many people can you make admire
a house whose every room you set on fire?
A hundred guests. Not one I dared let stay.
What would they love if beauty fell away?

IV. THE ABSENCE
Sibyl, I loved the roles you used to play,
then punished you when love got in their way.
Basil, you saw a soul beneath my skin.
I could not bear the truth you painted in.
Do not mistake my sorrow for repair.
I call their names. No answer anywhere.
I miss the ordinary life I fled:
a hand to hold, a book beside the bed.
A face allowed to change and still be dear.
Someone to watch the years with, year by year.

V. THE RETURN
I raise the knife against the painted stain,
as if a wound could cancel out the pain.
But nothing leaves us merely out of sight.
I hid the evidence. I could not make it right.
The canvas keeps the face I tried to save.
The years come home.
My body is their grave.

I wanted time to pass without a trace.
I should have asked for more than just a face.

Halloween lands on a Saturday for the first time since 2020, and Sunday is full of season finales. This is the weekend car season says goodbye, so make it count.

Saturday

1. Trunk or Treat by @cardadsclub and @legitmanila.chicago, 9 AM to 1 PM at the Bartlett Metra station lot. Awards for Best Costume, Best Trunk, and Best Group, free coffee and cocoa, and toy donations shipping to the Philippines before Christmas.

2. Halloween Car Show at the Gold Pyramid, 9 AM to 2 PM in Wadsworth. $20 mandatory registration starting at 8:30 AM, with awards for Best Costume (adult and child), Best Halloween Ride, Best Stock, Modified, and Truck, and top decorated rides, plus trunk and treat. Food and drinks available from Texas BBQ El Jefe.

Sunday

1. @motorcarsofchicago 3rd Annual Cars & Coffee, 9 AM to 12 PM at 3301 Essington Rd, Joliet. Show car parking runs 8 to 9 AM only, and the showroom opens at 9. Shirts, coffee, and donuts, plus a special appearance by Red Bull 😂.

2. The @fuelfedcarclub OPEN, 9 to 11 AM at 227 Northgate St, Lake Forest. Cars are parked by country: French, German, Italian, Swedish, and more. Free for spectators, with a suggested $20 donation for non-members showing a car.

3. Tuner Fest 2026 Closer by @stancedownlow, 12 to 5 PM at the Kane County Cougars stadium, Geneva. Spectators $10, car meet or VIP $20 per vehicle, showcase $30 per vehicle.

Which one are you hitting? Let me know in the comments.

#repost @cnn: New York City’s Central Park horse-drawn carriage industry is nearing its end after Mayor Zohran Mamdani and City Council Speaker Julie Menin reached a deal on legislation that aims to abolish the carriage rides.

Menin is expected to bring legislation to the council floor for a vote this month, a spokesperson told CNN.

The move comes after years of criticism from animal rights advocates who charge that the horses are overworked, get easily scared and live in inadequate stables with drivers flouting city regulations. Horse and carriage owners have denied the the claims, arguing the animals are well cared for and the stables are up to code.

The death of 18-year-old tourist Romanch Mahajan, who was killed after jumping from a runaway horse-drawn carriage in Central Park last summer, renewed calls to ban the century-old attraction. Mahajan is believed to be the first person to have died in a carriage accident since the rides were introduced more than 150 years ago, according to the industry’s labor union and the Central Park Conservancy, which manages the park.

A Clockwork Orange (1971), directed by Stanley Kubrick, is a true classic and a dream for architecture and design lovers. It keeps you on edge with its unsettling story and constant sense of tension, while visually mixing brutalist architecture, bold interiors, pop art, futuristic furniture and incredibly considered compositions. Kubrick used real modernist buildings around London—especially Thamesmead—and turned them into a strange, dystopian vision of the future. And the Korova Milk Bar alone is worth watching for: sculptural furniture, surreal interiors and unapologetically bold design. It’s one of those films where you might pause every few minutes just to look at the space.

The house feels almost as eccentric as the people living in it, with each room bringing its own combination of art, materials and unexpected design choices. The architecture also works beautifully with the story, creating spaces for gatherings, secrets and, of course, a little chaos. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ :🌶️🌶️🌶️🌶️

Tyler Carter Jennings has spent his life protecting the Ravenhood while conveniently ignoring his own emotional baggage. Enter Larissa DiCicco, a woman with dangerous family ties who needs his protection. Unfortunately for Tyler, she’s not exactly the type to sit quietly and follow instructions.

I spent half this book wanting to hug Tyler and the other half wanting to throw him through a window. The man needs therapy, a vacation, and possibly a restraining order against his own bad decisions. 

And Larissa, she gives it right back. Watching these two stubborn people try to navigate their feelings while actively making everything worse was exhausting in the most entertaining way. The chemistry was CHEMISTRYING, but someone needed to confiscate their ability to communicate because clearly neither of them knew how to use it.

Now, I won’t pretend this book didn’t test my patience. It’s LONG, and some of the family drama had me wondering if we’d ever get back to the romance. But the angst, the twists, and Tyler’s character development made the emotional marathon worth it.

Tropes:

🐦‍⬛ Enemies to lovers
🔥 Forced proximity
🖤 Morally gray MMC
💔 Wounded hero
🫂 Found family
🥀 Love after loss
🔪 Organized crime

Thank you @authorkatestewart and @kensingtonbooks for the #gifted ARC! 💚

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ | 🌶️🌶️🌶️

Saige is a bookbinder drowning in debt who somehow ends up imprisoned by immortals. Her only way out is making a deal with Archer, a cursed immortal general who needs her help restoring an ancient magical book. Honestly, being a book girl has never sounded more stressful. 😂

Archer is a grumpy, centuries-old immortal with black flames and the emotional availability of a brick wall. Naturally, I was invested. I loved the banter between him and Saige, but the mystery surrounding the ancient book and all the secrets slowly unraveling were what really kept me reading.

One thing I especially appreciated was Saige’s chronic pain representation. It’s not often we see a romantasy heroine dealing with chronic pain without it being magically cured or treated as a weakness. Such a refreshing detail that made me appreciate her character even more.

Tropes:

🔥 Forced proximity
☀️ Grumpy x sunshine
🗡️ Touch her and die

🐌 Slow burn

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ | 🌶️

Cat escaped a miserable marriage, became a pirate tavern owner, and was doing just fine until the Empire decided to ruin her life. Now she’s being forced to betray Valerian, a notorious pirate captain who also happens to be the one man she’s never gotten over.

I had a really good time with this one! The pirate setting, political drama, and all the messy history between Cat and Valerian made for such an interesting read. I especially loved the dual timelines and getting little pieces of their past as the story unfolded.

The pacing was a bit slow in places, and I would’ve loved more romance, but the tension and yearning definitely made up for some of that. There’s something about two people who clearly have unfinished business but are determined to make everything as complicated as humanly possible. 😂

🏴‍☠️ Pirates
❤️ Second-chance romance
🔥 Slow burn
⚔️ Political intrigue
🗡️ Betrayal & revenge

Lightwing picks up with Ferris trapped in a dark castle surrounded by Hollows and at the mercy of Hendrix Bane, a Fae who has quite literally marked her for death. She has an impossible task to complete, he absolutely hates her, and somehow they’re going to have to work together.

Enemies to lovers, a dark castle full of necromancy, a ruthless FMC, a black-hearted Fae, dark humor AND spice. AND it’s written by the Twisted Sisters, so I’m already mentally preparing myself to be emotionally abused by the cliffhanger…(the sisters never bestow mercy on their readers)

Briar leaves L.A. behind for a fresh start in the small mountain town of Crimson Ridge, only to find herself sharing an isolated cabin with Storm, a former pro bull rider who is very much off limits.

The tension in this one was SO good. Storm’s filthy mouth alone deserves its own rating 🫣I loved the whole “we absolutely should not be doing this” energy, especially when you throw forced proximity and one bed into the mix.

And underneath all of that, Storm was actually so sweet and protective with Briar. This was spicy, easy to fly through, and exactly the kind of forbidden romance I wanted.

[{'caption': '🌟 First TOS Guest Star for 2025 — From a hotel room in Thailand! 🇹🇭✨⁣ 
 
Beyond excited to hit this huge milestone in my career 🎉 But more importantly, I’m sharing this to say: Take the trip ✈️. Go to the wedding 💍, the birthday 🎂, the random weekend getaway. Plan your own wedding 💐. Whatever it is... Live your life 💫⁣ 
⁣ 
Because that’s exactly what I did. And ironically, one of my biggest bookings to date came from a self-tape I shot in a hotel room— with less-than-ideal lighting, an ironing board + stacked suitcases as my setup, and a janky little contraption to keep my phone upright for 2–3 takes. 
⁣ 
Oh—and I fumbled the last line. Instead of chasing perfection with another take, I sent it in.⁣ I knew the work was good. I trusted the CD and powers that be will see a real, living, breathing human being. Stop trying to be perfect.⁣ 
⁣ 
Even wilder? The shoot date was one day after we were to fly back home. I used to be terrified to leave town—missing vacations, events, moments—just in case something came up. I’ve missed out on far too many important events in my life and in the lives of my loved ones. Don’t be like past me.⁣ 
⁣ 
Trust that what’s meant for you will find you. Even across the world 🌍, with spotty Wi-Fi 📶 and a suitcase light setup. 💼💡⁣Trust. 🙏 Especially now, when the state of the industry feels uncertain. 🎭⁣ 
⁣ 
When it’s meant for you—it’s yours. Period.⁣

[{'caption': '🚀 Tesla has finally revealed the next-generation Roadster, and its headline feature is something almost no production car has ever attempted: it can actually leave the ground.

Tesla’s new halo car combines SpaceX-developed cold-gas thrusters with high-powered fans and suction technology, allowing the prototype to climb an inverted ramp, rotate through the air and land back on the pavement.

During the reveal, Tesla also demonstrated the Roadster lifting itself over several of the company’s vehicles while moving.

Acceleration is equally ridiculous, with the demonstrated car reportedly hitting 0–60 mph in just 0.81 seconds and Tesla claiming a top speed above 230 mph.

The redesigned two-seater also features steer-by-wire, an active retractable rear wing and aerospace-inspired propulsion hardware that makes the Roadster feel more like an engineering experiment than a traditional EV supercar.

After being originally revealed back in 2017 and delayed repeatedly, Tesla is currently targeting production around 2028, although the final road-legal specification could differ from the prototype shown.

Is this the most insane production-car concept Tesla has ever built?

What are your thoughts? 🤔💭

[{'caption': 'How to achieve the OG Taylor Swift curis, but make it heatless! Comment SWIFT and I will send you the link to the heatless curler.

1. Start with a zigzag part for a more natural curl pattern. This will also create the most volume!
2. Lightly mist dry hair with water. It’s important that the hair goes from damp to dry to allow the curls to truly set. You also don’t want the hair overly damp or the hair won’t dry all the way causing the curls to fall.
3. Prep the hair with a mousse for frizz control and extra hold.
4. Detangle the hair for smooth curls.
5. Grab your favorite heatless curler and clip in place.
6. Choose your wrap method! We used the add in method and wrapped each strip individually. For softer curls you can wrap 2 strips together.
**I like to twist the hair the opposite direction as I am wrapping it around the strip. This helps lock in layers and give extra definition to the curls.
7. Secure the ends with the elastic. I like to wrap the remainder of the strip around the end,and then secure with the elastic so the ends of the hair don’t get kinked.
8. Let the curls set overnight! Use a silk bonnet or pillowcase to help minimize frizz.
9. Release the curls! The best part! 🙌🏻
10. Style the curls! We like to gently separate each curl for added fullness.
11. Finish with your favorite oil for added shine and hydration!
12. Rock your gorgeous hair! 😊

i had lived with mental illness. there are parts of my childhood and my life that changed the way i learned to see myself, other people, safety, love and the future.

suicidal ideation can be incredibly quiet. it can exist alongside happy days, friendships, relationships, trips, birthdays and an entire life being lived.

[{'caption': 'The Cosmonaut Who Fell Home Backwards

His capsule hit the atmosphere the wrong way round, and he kept talking into a tape recorder the whole way down.

January 1969: Boris Volynov was alone in Soyuz 5 when the engine section failed to separate before reentry. Its solar panels held the whole stack hatch-first in the fire. Two years earlier he had helped investigate Vladimir Komarov's fatal parachute failure, so he narrated every detail for the investigators. Then the tanks behind him exploded.

Two beams from one black hole stretch 23 million light-years, and they should have torn apart long ago.

In 2024 astronomers mapping the cosmic web with the LOFAR radio telescope found Porphyrion: twin jets so long that one beam from our galaxy would reach Andromeda more than four times over. They kept firing for about two billion years, pushing into the near-empty voids between strands of galaxies, and beams like these may help explain why even the voids are magnetized.

A moon just 500 km wide is spraying its ocean into space, and one spacecraft flew right through it.

Enceladus, a tiny ice moon of Saturn, hides a global ocean under its shell. In 2015 Cassini dove 49 km above its south pole and sampled the spray: salt, silica grains that form in hot water, and hydrogen that microbes on Earth live on. Phosphorus later turned up in the E ring its spray built. Then NASA had to decide what to do with Cassini.

Two spacewalkers bolted a human skeleton to the station's hull, then went back inside without it.

It was Matroshka, a European radiation experiment: a real skeleton cast in tissue-like plastic, sliced into 33 layers, packed with thousands of crystal detectors and sealed in a shell about as protective as a spacesuit. It stayed outside the International Space Station for 539 days, from February 2004 to August 2005, to measure how much radiation reaches an astronaut's organs. The spacewalkers and crew shown are illustrative, not the real crew.

The capsule came down right on target, but the three men inside had died far above, in space.

June 1971: the Soyuz 11 crew were returning from three weeks aboard Salyut 1, the first space station. At 168 km, the bolts that separate the capsule fired all at once, and the jolt shook open a tiny valve. Their air rushed out into space in seconds. Alexei Leonov, who should have commanded the flight, later tried closing that valve himself.

You've climbed the tallest mountain in the solar system, and it looks like a parking lot.

Olympus Mons on Mars stands about 22 km high but is about 600 km across, the size of Italy. Mars is small, so your horizon is only about 3 km away, and over 3 km the summit barely drops. The hard part is the edge: a cliff up to 8 km tall. Earth can't build a mountain like this because its plates carry each volcano off the hot spot; Mars has no moving plates, so the lava kept stacking until the summit rose above almost all of the air. In 1971, Mariner 9 found Mars buried in a global dust storm. Only a few dark spots poked through, and the biggest was Olympus Mons.

The astronaut is imagined; nobody has stood on Olympus Mons. Diagrams compress time and exaggerate vertical scale; terrain heights come from NASA MOLA data.

A perfectly straight streak in a Hubble image looked like a camera glitch. It was 200,000 light-years long.

The line shoots out of a distant galaxy and is made of young stars. It was built for the hottest, most crushing planet in the solar system, and spent 53 years stuck circling ours.

In 1972 the Soviet Union launched two Venus landers four days apart. One reached Venus and radioed from the surface for 50 minutes. The other’s engine shut off early and left it in Earth orbit, while empty tanks from its rocket fell red-hot onto New Zealand farms. In May 2025 the lander finally came down, with a parachute sized for Venus’s thick air.

Illustrative 3D reconstruction: nobody saw the reentry or impact, and the capsule has not been found.

Aim a rocket straight at the Sun and it misses. Earth carries everything on it sideways around the Sun at about 30 km/s. To hit the Sun, a spacecraft must cancel almost all of that motion. NASA's Parker Solar Probe used seven Venus flybys as brakes; on Christmas Eve 2024 it passed about 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface at roughly 692,000 km/h. Orbits in this film are not to scale and time is compressed.

Sources: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, 'It's Surprisingly Hard to Go to the Sun' (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/13017); NASA Science, 'A Big Year for Our Sun' (science.nasa.gov/sun/helio-big-year); Johns Hopkins APL Parker Solar Probe mission pages.

The biggest thing ever built in space is going to end in the ocean, and NASA is paying SpaceX to make sure of it.

After 25 years with people aboard, the International Space Station is ageing and leaking. It can’t be flown home in pieces, left to fall wherever drag takes it, pushed higher into the junk, or blown up. So a modified Dragon, built under a contract worth up to $843 million, will drive it steeply into the remote South Pacific near Point Nemo, where most of it burns up and the rest sinks.

Shut your eyes on the space station and the dark starts flashing: dots, streaks, even a blue diamond.

Astronauts have reported the flashes since Apollo 11. Later Apollo crews ran sessions in the dark, some blindfolded, and counted about one flash every three minutes; Apollo 15’s commander saw one “like a blue diamond.” Their eyes were fine. The cause comes from far outside the solar system, and it passes straight through them. Linking the blue diamond to Cherenkov light is our interpretation; scientists still debate how much each mechanism contributes.

Sources: Nancy Atkinson, “Seeing Cosmic Rays in Space” (NASA reprint, 2012); Don Pettit, “Flashes of Reality,” Air & Space; Apollo crew reports on cosmic-ray visual phenomena.

The first time, we sold it conditionally, but the bank appraisal came back unbelievably low. I challenged it, presented the facts, and fought for a second appraisal. The second came back better, but it was still too low.

But I didn’t give up.

We brought the property back to the market, and I SOLD IT AGAIN, conditionally, at a great price!

In today’s uncertain market, low bank appraisals are becoming a serious challenge. But just because a bank appraises your property at a certain value doesn’t automatically mean that’s what your home is worth.

A good Realtor knows how to challenge a low appraisal professionally, present comparable sales, provide market evidence, and fight for a fair assessment.

And remember: A conditional sale is not a closed sale. Financing and appraisal conditions matter, and you need a Realtor who knows how to handle setbacks and protect your interests.

That’s what I do. I don’t just put a sign on the lawn and hope for the best. I stand behind my sellers, defend their property’s value, negotiate hard, and find solutions.

[{'caption': 'I take back what I said in this video👇🏽

1. I said “I like not knowing the prices” but then the bill came and we unknowingly ordered two drinks that were $120 and a dessert for my birthday that was $140. The total bill for the meal including tip was $926.86 😳. If the food was incredible, it would have been worth it. But the food wasn’t anything extraordinary (except for the beef Wellington). Because I estimated $500 for this specific meal so part of me does wish I had a menu with all of the prices on it tbh

2. HOWEVER, we set aside a specific amount in our high yield savings account to cover food, shopping, and Ubers/taxis on the trip. It felt really freeing at the beginning of the meal to know that regardless of how much the bill was, we would have it covered because we planned for it.*

I definitely would have felt horrible if we were putting everything on a credit card and hoping for the best like the last time we were in Italy. 

3. I loved getting to sit there and enjoy my birthday while my husband was thinking about the prices. It was really refreshing and i wish more restaurants did this!

I’m disappointed this meal was expensive but didn’t feel “worth it”  but… proud of us for being financially prepared? Also, would this of happened if the prices were on my menu? 🤔🤣

A clip marked with CCTV (China’s state TV) logos depicts a missile launching from a desert site, with an inset showing a rail-mounted ship-shaped target, followed by a large fireball engulfing a carrier-like mock-up on the sand. 

Online accounts have identified the weapon as the DF-26B, the anti-ship variant of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force’s Dongfeng-26 intermediate-range ballistic missile.

My family loves a good soup night! 🥣 

Ingredients:

•3 pounds of russet or yellow potatoes (cubed)
•4 ribs of celery (diced)
•4 medium carrots (diced)
•1 large onion (diced)
•1 1/2 tbsp minced garlic 
•4 tbsp butter
•2 tbsp olive oil
•1/3 cup flour
•16 oz of ham steak
•8 cups chicken broth
•2 cups water
•2 cups heavy cream
•paprika
•salt and pepper to taste

Directions:

• heat your pot on medium heat and add your butter and olive oil

• add your onion, carrots, celery and sauté until soft

• once the veggies begin to soften, add your garlic and cook for one minute

•add about a tsp of salt and about 1/4 tsp of pepper

• then add your flour and mix until the flour is combined

• pour in your chicken broth, water, and heavy cream, and bring to a boil 

• once boiling, add your potatoes and ham and cook on medium/medium low heat until potatoes are soft and tender

• then taking a wooden spoon or a masher, mash some of the potatoes at the bottom of your pot to create a thicker consistency for the soup

Must save. Healthy & perfect for the season 🍌🍂🍁🍃

Made with spelt flour, naturally sweetened with ripe bananas, and full of chocolatey goodness. So easy, so delicious!

Ingredients:
🍌 4 ripe bananas, roughly mashed
🥚 1 egg
🤎 ¾ cup spelt flour
✨ 1 tsp vanilla extract
✨ 1 tsp baking soda
🍫 Chocolate chips, as much as your heart desires
🤎 Cinnamon, to taste
🧂 A pinch of coarse salt
🍁 Pure maple syrup, optional (if your bananas aren’t sweet enough)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. Roughly mash the bananas, leaving some chunks for extra texture.
3. Add the egg and vanilla extract and mix.
4. Stir in the spelt flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
5. Fold in the chocolate chips. Taste your bananas beforehand to decide whether you’d like to add a little pure maple syrup.
6. Pour into a lined loaf pan and bake until the center is set and a toothpick comes out without wet batter, approximately 45–60 minutes.
7. Let it cool slightly, slice and ENJOY!

The secret? Really ripe bananas and not overmixing the batter.

It is absolutely yum!! 😋 

French Onion Pot Roast
(serves 5-6)

- 2.5-3 lb chuck roast
- salt and pepper
- olive oil
- 1/2 stick butter (4 tbsps)
- 2 large yellow onions sliced
- 8 oz baby bella mushrooms sliced 
- 5 cloves garlic minced
- 1 tbsp flour
- 1/4 cup sherry cooking wine
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce 
- 3 cups beef broth
- 8 oz bag shredded mozzarella or provolone 

Directions:

Preheat the oven to 325.

Season the beef chuck on all sides with salt and pepper.

Add olive oil to a large heat safe casserole pot or dutch oven and heat to medium. Once hot, sear the beef on both sides until golden brown and set aside. 

Add the butter to the pot, once melted, add the sliced onions and season with a pinch of salt. Sauté for about 10 minutes until  softened then add the mushrooms and garlic and sauté for 5-7 minutes then add the flour. Cook the flour for a minute or two and add the sherry wine, thyme, bay leaves, worcestershire sauce, a dash of black pepper and beef broth. Stir well with a wooden spatula, making sure to scrape the bottom to release the browned bits.

Carefully place the beef chuck in along with its juices, ladle over the broth, onions and mushrooms and cover.

Place in the oven and braise for 3 hours.

Once done, remove from oven, skim out some of the oil and fat that’s floated to the top and shred the beef. 

Top with the shredded cheese and place back in the oven. Broil for 3-5 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbly.

Enjoy with your favorite sides: roasted veggies, mashed potatoes, crusty bread, etc!

My version is slightly more simplified as I used more of what I had on hand but still amazing nonetheless! 😋

Ina Garten’s Creamy Mustard Chicken
(serves 4)

- olive oil
- 4 bone in chicken thighs
- salt and pepper
- 1 onion sliced
- splash white wine
- 7.5 oz crème fraiche 
- 1 heaping tbsp stone ground dijon mustard

Directions:

Salt and pepper both sides of the chicken.

In a large skillet, heat the olive oil to medium to medium high and place the chicken skin side down and set timer for 15 minutes. Flip the chicken and set the timer for another 15 minutes and add in the onions, moving them between the chicken.

Once done, remove and set aside the chicken.

Pour in a splash of white wine and continue to caramelize the onion until golden brown.

Add the crème fraiche and mustard, stir well and season to taste with salt and pepper if needed.

Put the chicken back in, skin side up, along with its juices and simmer for an additional 5-7 minutes making sure not to touch the skin with the sauce to keep it crispy!

Enjoy with your favorite sides!

Philly Cheesesteak Pot Roast
(serves 5-6)

- 2.5-3 lb beef chuck
- 1 onion sliced
- 2 green bell peppers sliced
- salt and pepper
- 1/2 tsp seasoning salt (I used Johnny’s)
- olive oil
- 5 cloves minced garlic
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter 
- 1 tbsp flour
- 1 tbsp tomato paste 
- 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce 
- 1 cup red wine
- 2 cups beef broth
- sliced provolone cheese

Directions:

Preheat oven to 325.

Salt and pepper the beef chuck. In a shallow oven safe pot or dutch oven, sear the meat on medium high heat in olive oil until golden brown on both sides and set aside.

Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, garlic and tomato paste. Cook for about 2 minutes then add the flour and cook for another minute. 

Pour in the red wine, making sure to scrape the brown bits from the bottom with a wooden spatula. Allow the alcohol to cook out for about 2-3 minutes and add the worcestershire, beef broth, thyme, bay leaf, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper.

Carefully add the beef back in, ladle over some of the broth, then cover and braise for 3 hours.

Meanwhile, in a new pan, sauté the onions and bell pepper in olive oil on medium heat and season with your fave seasoning salt (I used Johnny’s). Cook for 7-10 minutes  or until just softened and set aside.

Once the beef is done cooking, remove from oven, shred the meat, then mix in the onions and bell peppers.

Now layer on the provolone cheese and set back in the oven to broil for about 3-5 minutes until golden and bubbly.

I have been influenced by @cocolarkincooks - her Chicken Au Poivre looked so incredibly delicious that I had to recreate it, with just a few tweaks to make it my own. Trust me, this is going to be your new favorite roast chicken recipe! 🤩

Chicken Au Poivre
(serves 4-5)

- 1 whole chicken (around 4lbs)
- olive oil
- salt
- 1 1/2 tbsp fresh ground black peppercorns
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 1 tbsp fresh rosemary minced (or 1/2 tbsp dried)
- 1 shallot diced
- 5 cloves garlic minced
- 1/4 cup dry sherry cooking wine
- 1 head cauliflower florets
- 8 oz baby bella mushrooms sliced
- beurre manié (1 tbsp softer butter + 1 tbsp flour mixed into a smooth paste)

Directions:

Preheat oven to 375.

Spatchcock the chicken by removing the backbone and flattening it (save the bone in the freezer for another day to make bone broth) and pat dry with a paper towel.

Place chicken in a large casserole dish or pot, drizzle olive oil on both sides and season generously with salt and tuck in the wings (so they don’t burn). Roast in oven for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, prep the sauce by mixing together the heavy cream, shallot, garlic, rosemary, cracked black pepper, 1 tsp salt and sherry wine.

Once the 20 minutes is up, carefully set aside the chicken and add the cauliflower and mushrooms to the pot. Place the check on top and pour the sauce all over the chicken.

Place back in the oven and cook for an additional 1 hour (or until the meat thermometer reads 165) - making sure to baste the chicken with the sauce every 20 minutes.

Once done, carefully removing the chicken onto a cutting board to rest and place the pot on the stove on medium heat.

Add the beurre manié to the sauce and stir well to melt and to thicken the sauce, about 5 minutes, adjust seasoning adding a pinch of salt if needed and remove from heat.

Cut the chicken and serve on top of the sauced up cauliflower and mushrooms and enjoy!

The lawsuit is the latest attempt to stop the 250-foot-tall arch, which Trump hopes to build near Arlington National Cemetery and says will commemorate the nation’s 250th birthday. The administration would like to begin construction as soon as Nov. 5.

The two jurisdictions argue that they have “indisputable standing” to bring their lawsuit because the towering arch would have tangible, negative effects on the region — an argument that distinguishes their lawsuit from others that have tried to stop Trump’s construction projects.

D.C. Attorney General Brian Schwalb (D) said the arch construction would cause “serious, immediate and irreparable harm to the District and its residents,” while Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones (D) said “Trump’s illegal vanity project” would be an affront to Arlington National Cemetery and the “extraordinary sacrifices it represents.”

In a separate case brought by three Vietnam War veterans and a historic preservationist, a federal judge on Friday signaled she might block it.

Probably not…😬

Other than caffeine, none of the ingredients in one sugar-free energy drink come even remotely close to a dose you should worry about

Even the next highest dosed ingredient that has been linked to any negative health outcome (Ace-K), is still even 1/4,000th of the highest dose tested in research that’s STILL been shown to be safe

I’m not promoting these as a “health” drink

But the fear around them is wildly misplaced

Caffeine is by far the biggest concern for your heart if you’re not paying attention to your total daily intake

One can only has 150mg, which isn’t bad on it’s own

But stack that with a coffee in the morning, another in the afternoon, and pre-workout later, and your total can easily creep past the recommended 400mg a day

And over time that puts exess stress on your heart, blood pressure, and nervous system 

You don’t have to drink these

Actually, yeah…

3 well organized, and intense sessions per week can absolutely make more progress than 4, 5, or even 6 days that aren’t put together well

That doesn’t mean you should never consider training past that though

As you get more advanced you might benefit from more total sets throughout the week, and extra days can make that easier to fit in without turning every workout into a marathon

They can also help if you’re so tired by the end of your sessions that the exercises later in your workout are constantly suffering

But what matters most is:

- how consistent you can be while still training hard (the actual quality of your workouts)
- whether you’re able to hit each muscle group multiple times throughout the week
- whether you enjoy the routine enough to stick with it
- and whether you’re actually making progress over time

How well (or not-so-well) you’re doing on those is what determines how many days you’d probably make the most progress with

For a lot of people 3-4 hard, well-structured sessions are enough to make incredible progress without needing to spend more days in the gym

But what makes them stubborn, is that these fat cells have a higher density of what’s called alpha-2-receptors on them, and that makes them more resistant to letting go of stored fat to use as energy

But that fat doesn’t defy physics. You can still lose it, you just can’t choose where it comes off first

As you lose fat, some areas will change more quickly than others, and those “stubborn” areas will just take longer to show up

Losing stubborn fat really comes down to two things:

1. Being in big enough of a calorie deficit
2. And being in that deficit long enough to actually reach those slower changing areas 

There’s no hack, supplement, or workout that lets you target or choose where the fat comes off first

Kind of a lot…

There’s a ton of other things that impact how hard a lift is besides height (muscle mass, insertions, joint angles, limb proportions, technique, etc.)

But height and frame impact lifting/physique in 4 main ways:

1. Shorter lifters usually have a lot higher *relative* strength compared to taller lifters. The leverage is better on most lifts so the same weight is just way easier to move

2. aller lifters usually have a higher ceiling for muscle growth. Since the size of your frame determines how much muscle your body can physically support, the potential for how much total muscle they can build is just higher

3. Gaining muscle on a smaller frame usually looks a LOT more impressive (and a lot quicker) compared to a taller athlete gaining the same amount of muscle (e.g. 10lbs of muscle fills out a shorter frame a lot more than it does on a taller one)

4. Longer limbs = longer bar path = more work done each rep. For taller lifters the weight just has to physically travel further, and that requires more force to move, and because of this taller lifters usually fatigue faster doing the same reps as someone shorter

That’s why for taller clients I’ll often adjust rep ranges slightly lower compared to shorter one’s (e.g. 3–5 reps vs 4–8 reps, 8-10 reps vs. 10-12 reps, etc.)

So there’s pro’s and con’s for both, you just have to learn to work with what you’ve got

July | Online Community

This is more than a book club. This is a structured anti-racism learning space created by Day and Brandi for white women who are ready to learn, unlearn, reflect, and take action.

For nearly 2 years, this community has grown to more than 150 members. Together, members read one book each month, join monthly discussions, watch documentaries and TED Talks, complete reflection work, and participate in deeper conversations that move beyond surface-level learning.

The program is $22 per month, about $5.50 per week. Scholarships are available for members who cannot afford the monthly membership fee.

The 3-year journey includes:

Year 1: Actor Level
Identify performative actions, uncover new ways to raise awareness, and begin the internal work.

Year 2: Ally Level
Deepen your education, amplify Black voices, and learn how to leverage privilege for advocacy.

Year 3: Accomplice Level
Use your privilege to actively fight racism and injustice through real action.

Members also receive tools for deeper learning, including journaling prompts, conversation starters, quarterly quizzes, a private Facebook group, monthly orientation meetings, yearly in-person events, quarterly fireside chats, and special conversations.

This space is led by Black women and designed specifically for white women because white women are uniquely positioned to challenge racism in their homes, workplaces, friendships, and communities.

Join the club: bookclubs.com/anti-racism-book-club-13/join/
Or click the link in my bio.

Scholarship information: AntiRacismscholarship@gmail.com

[{'caption': 'If you’re new here, HI! We’d love to introduce ourselves. And if you’ve been here a while, thank you for sticking around and for loving, supporting, and encouraging our family along the way. We’re so grateful for every one of you who follows our journey!

Devon and I have been married for 26 years, and we have four kids: Taylor, Luke, Blake, and Jack. Taylor is married to Kayden, our son-in-law. And Jack is the youngest. He has Down syndrome, and we like to tell everyone he’s the rock star of our family, because no one really cares about the rest of us, haha. They just want to talk to Jack 🫶🏻☺️

When Jack was born, we had no idea he would have Down syndrome. As I tried to picture what our life would look like, I came across a YouTube video of a young man with Down syndrome who made a day-in-the-life video for his senior project. He rode his bike to the YMCA to swim laps, came home and made himself a smoothie, walked the dog, and went to the movies with his friends. He did it all on his own.

After watching it, I remember thinking: if Jack’s life can look anything like his, everything is going to be okay.

When we started sharing our lives here and as our videos began to gain traction, I realized I could do the same thing for someone else. I could give other families a glimpse into their future. I could show them the joy that people with Down syndrome bring into our lives and everything they’re capable of.

I love advocating for Jack and sharing the moments of inclusion we’ve had at school and with his friends. I’m so grateful for the ripple effect it’s had, both in our community and around the world, as parents watch these videos and talk with their kids about including others and being a friend to someone who needs a friend, even someone who has special needs. 🤍😄

We’d love to get to know you in the comments below 👇🏼
