[{'caption': 'I am delighted to announce The Economist Insider. 

With our new video product we will be lifting the curtain on our journalists and the spirited and constructive debates we have around critical global issues. These conversations have been kept largely within our editorial meetings—now we are inviting our subscribers inside. 

From next month I will be joined by Edward Carr, our deputy editor, every Thursday in The Insider, a weekly show in which we explore the news and trends shaping the world now—and what comes next.

I’m also looking forward to inviting global leaders to challenge our point of view and discuss the big issues shaping a tumultuous world.

[{'caption': 'Most of your life outcomes are decided by a handful of choices you make early on, yet we rarely treat them with the seriousness they deserve.

Where you live determines the people you meet, the ideas you’re exposed to, and the opportunities that find you.

Who you choose to be with affects your emotional baseline, your ambition, and the kind of life you build day after day.

What you decide to work on shapes your skills, your leverage, and the trajectory of your career.

These decisions quietly compound for years, even decades, but we often rush into them while spending enormous time dealing with their consequences.

If something is going to dominate your life for five, ten, or twenty years, it’s worth slowing down and thinking deeply about it.

That requires freeing up time, saying no to noise, and resisting the world’s constant pressure to stay busy.
Clarity doesn’t come from movement it comes from space.

This is the kind of long-term thinking Naval Ravikant emphasizes: don’t optimize for short-term comfort, optimize for the decisions that shape your future.

Utah has a coal plant that was never allowed to die. The coal units at the Intermountain Power Project near Delta stopped running last year when new gas units took over, so the lights never went out. But the Legislature passed a law blocking anyone from decommissioning them. They’ve been kept in working order, like a truck on blocks, waiting for a buyer.

On November 4, a committee picks that buyer from four secret bids. Every bidder signed a nondisclosure agreement, and state officials confirmed to lawmakers that the public can’t see a single offer. The state gets the final say, and it can even buy the coal units itself with your money.

Who wants a 40-year-old coal plant? At least one data center developer in Delta has said publicly it wants these units to power a giant AI campus. That campus has one small tenant and is hunting for big ones. If no big customer shows up, nobody restarts the coal.

So here’s my question for OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Google, Amazon and xAI. You’ve all promised that AI won’t run on dirty power or on the backs of families’ electric bills. Ted Cruz said it on his own podcast (Verdict, Oct 30): if Republicans lose the 8 to 10 close races, "we could wake up the day after Election Day instead of 53 Republicans with 45." He also called the early vote "a bloodbath."

The math: 53 − 8 = 45. Republicans would have to lose eight of their seats and win none back.

The map (270toWin averages, Oct 31): Democrats lead in six Republican seats. North Carolina +11.6, Kansas +3.8, Ohio +3.5, Texas +3.2, Maine +2.6, Alaska +2.2. Iowa: Republicans +0.6. That's seven. The eighth would be Nebraska (Ricketts +2.0 over independent Osborn) or South Carolina (Graham +2.4).

The markets (Oct 31): Kalshi's seat-count market prices 45 or fewer at 27¢, about 1 in 4. Its middle guess: 47. (Senate control: Kalshi 71% Democrats, Polymarket 70.5%.)

The Republicans' best case: in 2014, Senate polls overrated Democrats by 4 points on average (FiveThirtyEight). Misses go both ways, though. And Cruz isn't forecasting: in the same breath he tells listeners "there are Republican votes out there to turn that around."

Moved since we made this (Nov 1): Ohio tightened to Brown +2.0, Maine widened to Jackson +3.6, Nebraska is Ricketts +2.6, and Kalshi's 45-or-fewer fell to 22¢.

Verdict: possible, not likely.

No opinion, just the numbers. Sources in the first comment.

I keep coming back to that trip now, reminiscing on every moment I didn’t know was the last.  We shared the same passion for climbing, and that's what our friendship was built on from the start. Lenni was one of those people you were just lucky to know. He had this way of making everything feel lighter just by being there. Generous with his time, his knowledge, his energy. He wanted to share the things he loved with as many people as possible, and that generosity was who he really was, not just the parts on camera. He never made anyone feel small. He had this rare ability to stay warm and present even in the hardest moments, the kind of moments that usually strip people down to their worst. He'd be smiling. And that's just the type of person he was.
I know that he wouldn't want his death to make the people who loved him afraid of the things he loved. He spent his time trying to bring people into what mattered to him, not close it off. As a son. A brother. A friend who showed up for people, again and again, in ways so many of you know better than I do. Every story I heard only confirmed what I already knew: he was deeply, deeply loved. He was loved by so many, and that love isn't going anywhere.

The two met in 1933 at Choate Preparatory School, becoming inseparable friends. They traveled together, exchanged hundreds of letters, and maintained a close relationship for approximately 30 years.

But there's another part of this story.

Lem Billings was gay, something he kept largely private during an era when homosexuality was heavily stigmatized.

And perhaps that's what makes their story so fascinating.

At a time when being openly gay could destroy someone's career and reputation, one of America's most famous presidents maintained an extraordinarily close friendship with a gay man.

The history of JFK and Lem Billings reminds us that LGBTQ+ people have always been part of American history, including the personal lives of some of its most powerful figures.

Before leaving the NICU floor on the way out, Rowdy had to stop at nearly every station to say goodbye. Nurse after nurse, doctor after doctor, all loving on our boy one last time. Our sweet Rowdy was truly so loved.

Seeing the “Thank You For Visiting” sign on the way out felt surreal after six long weeks of this place becoming our home.

Rowdy would have NEVER survived without his neonatal nurses. He would have never made it out of those hospital doors and into our arms at home without the incredible hands that cared for him, fought for him, and kept him alive when he couldn’t fight for himself. His survival was dependent on their knowledge, their quick decisions, their compassion, and their unwavering dedication..even our own survival was dependent on them..

Today, on International Neonatal Nurses Day, we will forever be grateful for the nurses who made bringing our baby home possible. And for so many that have to experience this, millions of babies are alive because of YOU, THANK YOU! You are worlds truest SUPERHEROS! 💙

1. Bought Palantir at $11.08\xa0in 2022. Held for two years. Sold at $15.98. Few months later I watched it explode. Did the technically correct thing and still lost.
2. Tried to be cool and play the hero for a random girl. Ended up getting into a fight with four guys outside a bar. Genuinely thought I’d win. Three days in the hospital with a shattered face and scars that won’t fade
3. Spent years smoking, doing drugs, numbing, and waiting for life to change on its own. Thought time would fix things. Turns out time just passes, whether you grow or not.
4. Played League of Legends for over a decade just to peak at Gold III. Ten years of wasting time just to confirm I have zero talent and terrible hand-eye coordination.
5. Got a Math degree from UofT thinking it meant I had direction. Ended up in tech sales. Quickly found out I’m not a natural killer. Just loud, talkative, and winging it.
6. Made decisions that derailed my life and forced me to face myself with no distractions, no excuses, no audience. Not proud of that chapter. Not ready to share it yet. But it stripped me down to the truth.
7. Spent most of my 20s thinking I was tougher, smarter, and more special than I was. Reality corrected me fast. Got scammed three times in four years. Lost over $40k and a little faith in humanity.

I’m 30 now.
Entry-level job.
No “ahead of schedule” milestones.
No cool narrative to sell.

And honestly?
I’ve been ashamed for most of my life, of who I am, where I’m at, and how far I still have to go. I hid it with jokes, detachment, and pretending I didn’t care.

But I care. A lot.

I’m tired of lying to myself.
Tired of waiting.
Tired of coping instead of building.

I don’t want a glow-up.
I want self-respect.

Discipline over comfort.
Consistency over motivation.
Ownership over excuses.

This isn’t a comeback post.
It’s a line in the sand.

If you’re 25, 30, 35 and feel behind. You’re not broken.
You’re just done lying to yourself.

And that’s where real change starts.

Not because I think I am better than anyone.

Even if I am not making money from this right now. Even if I am pouring time and energy into content while still broke.

George R.R. Martin repeatedly rejected film adaptations of A Song of Ice and Fire, believing the story was simply too vast for a movie and refusing offers to adapt only parts of it. When David Benioff and D.B. Weiss approached him about a television series, Martin famously tested them by asking who they believed Jon Snow’s mother was. Satisfied with their answer, he eventually agreed to sell them the rights.

Turning the books into Game of Thrones soon became an enormous undertaking, with the creators describing each season as essentially making a ten hour movie. Season five alone was filmed across five countries and 151 sets over 240 days, involving 166 cast members, more than 1,000 crew members, and over 5,000 extras. What began as a character driven drama grew into one of the largest and most ambitious television productions ever attempted.

2010:
19 years old. Started travelling.

2010:
Learning to survive with a Burmese hill tribe.

2011:
Working as a scuba instructor in Thailand.

2012:
Fighting Muay Thai in Thailand.

2013:
Training for a world-first expedition.

2014:
Became the first person to walk across Mongolia solo and unsupported.
78 days. 1,500 miles.

2015:
Broke. Rejected. Already working on the next project.

2016:
Became the first person ever to traverse the length of Madagascar.
155 days. 1,600 miles.

2017:
Still broke. Rejected by TV, brands, speaking opportunities and more.
Persistence and consistency mattered more than talent.

2018:
Training for the biggest challenge I’d ever attempted.

2019:
Became the first person to hike the entire 4,000-mile length of the Yangtze River across China.
352 days.

2019:
Invited onto The Joe Rogan Experience.

2020:
Walking the Yangtze launched on National Geographic.

2022:
Secured a multimillion-dollar TV series, The Great Wall with Ash Dykes.

2023:
Planning another world first.

2024:
Became part of the first team to travel source to sea of the Coppename River in Suriname.

2025:
Uncharted Amazon with Ash Dykes launched on Discovery Channel.

2025:
Secured an international TV series following the Yellow River by land, air and water across China.

2026:
Launching the biggest independent project of my life…

If there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s this:

Your future won’t be built by one big moment.
It will be built by thousands of ordinary days when you choose to keep going, even when nobody is watching.

Keep showing up.

c’è anche una storia oscura (che mi ha segnalato una di voi): Stanley Marsh 3, il finanziatore dell’opera, fu incriminato per abusi sessuali su minorenni. Morì nel 2014 prima del processo, senza una condanna per quelle accuse.

If it wasn’t already obvious, the Lamborghini Reventon is a tribute to the F-22 Raptor, and it was revealed in 2007 as a Murcielago-based few-off, powered by the same 6.5 liter V12. The exterior design is entirely different, penned by the legendary Filippo Perini, but underneath the bodywork it’s an LP-640, putting out only ten extra horsepower.

The biggest difference between the two is probably the price tag: while the Murcielago retailed for $350,000, the Reventon had a base price of $1,500,000, all while essentially being mechanically identical. It was Lamborghini’s first entry into their few-off program, which now includes cars like the Aventador-based Veneno.

This is a Ferrari 456 GT Venice Cabriolet, and it’s one of seven built for Prince Jefri Bolkiah, but only this example managed to escape Brunei, and because of that I can show you what makes it so special.

It’s based on the Ferrari 456 GT, but obviously, it’s a convertible, which wasn’t offered from factory. The rear seats were removed to make room for the roof, which was sourced from the R129 Mercedes SL, and the factory six speed manual transaxle was replaced by a Mercedes four speed auto. The interior is coated in Connolly leather, with seats taken straight from a BMW 8 Series, and forget green over tan, it’s green over green.

I stopped by @concourscollectionstorage in Los Angeles to check out the Lamborghini Sesto Elemento they have on site: one of around ten ever produced, and one of only two that’s certified for the street.

In 2011, this car was impossible. Loosely based on the Lamborghini Gallardo, it’s imbued with technology from the aerospace industry, and it was the first car to feature forged carbon fiber, which you can see absolutely everywhere. The interior is just a padded carbon tub, with no dashboard or digital aids. The exterior components are all carbon too, down to the exhaust tips and the wheels. Even the suspension is constructed from carbon, so the Sesto Elemento weighs just under one tonne, making it lighter than a Mazda Miata.

All of them were built for track use only, but @lanzantelimited in England offers a road legal conversion, and this one had the work done. With that, you get an AC system, a front axle lift, indicators, license plate brackets — it isn’t much, but it makes it registrable, and there’s definitely allure to having a road legal race car.

The Sesto Elemento was one of my childhood superheroes, and fifteen years later, it’s just as exciting.

The White-bellied Sea Eagle (*Haliaeetus leucogaster*) is a majestic bird of prey found along the coastlines and large inland water bodies of South and Southeast Asia, and Australia. This large eagle is easily identified by its striking white belly and head, contrasting with its dark grey wings and back. With a wingspan of up to 2.2 meters, it soars gracefully over water, hunting for fish, birds, and small mammals. Known for its powerful build and commanding presence, the White-bellied Sea Eagle is a symbol of strength and freedom.

@NASAWebb’s unique view of the stellar nursery known as NGC 7129 reveals numerous stars formerly hidden in this cosmic cauldron. 
 
Stars begin their life in cold, dense regions of dust and gas, hiding from view of most telescopes. Webb’s high degree of infrared sensitivity allows astronomers to peer through dust to study these baby stars. 
 
In this image, we can see stars in various stages of development. The most mature and massive (about 5-8x the mass of our Sun) is the region’s bright central star. In the cavity on the left, appearing in gold, is the largest demonstration of its impact. The outflows from an earlier stage in the star’s development carve into the dense molecular cloud of hydrogen, and combine with the star’s light, causing it to glow. 
 
The region on the right, represented in red, hides much younger objects than those on the left: protostars. As the protostars accumulate matter and increase mass, they eject outflows of super heated material that interact with matter around the star, creating shocks that cause the textured appearance we see in this image. More protostar outflows are at upper left where a dark shadow is being cast by a protostar disk, visible against the surrounding nebula, depicted in blue. 
 
Seeing these different structures help astronomers study the star lifecycle in various stages, leading to a more complete understanding of our universe. 

See more in the link in @NASAWebb’s bio.

[{'caption': 'I’m grateful for the opportunity to speak to the nation about maternal mental health—because this conversation cannot end when the headlines do.

Regardless of how you feel about the Lindsay Clancy case, it has forced us to confront something we have ignored for far too long: we are failing women. We are failing mothers.

We celebrate the baby and too often forget the person who gave birth.

We send women home after one of the most physically, hormonally, emotionally, and psychologically demanding experiences of their lives—and expect them to simply figure it out.

Postpartum depression, anxiety, and psychosis deserve more than awareness. We need research, screening, access to qualified mental health care, continuity of care, family education, and systems designed to recognize when a mother is struggling BEFORE she reaches a crisis.

And we need to stop treating maternal mental health as a personal failure when so much of what is failing is the system around her.

Supporting mothers is not a luxury.
Maternal mental health is not an afterthought.
And surviving pregnancy cannot be our only measure of success.

Women deserve to thrive.

I’m grateful to continue using my voice, my experience as an OB/GYN, and every platform available to keep this conversation moving forward.

Because we can—and must—do better for mothers.

We love telling new mothers, “Sleep when the baby sleeps.”

Okay… but WHO is doing everything else?

Who is washing the bottles, doing the laundry, making dinner, cleaning the kitchen, taking care of the other children?

Because if the answer is still MOM, when exactly is she supposed to sleep?

I learned how ridiculous the phrase “sleep when the baby sleeps” when I had my own baby. 

This isn’t just about being tired.
Sleep deprivation changes the brain.

It affects attention, working memory, impulse control, judgment and decision-making. It makes emotional regulation harder. 

And yet we have somehow normalized significant sleep deprivation as simply part of motherhood.

That is insane.

A woman grows a human, delivers a human, experiences enormous hormonal and physical changes, may be bleeding, breastfeeding, recovering from abdominal or vaginal surgery, managing pain and simultaneously learning how to keep another human alive…

…and somehow we expect her to keep running the household too.

No.

Postpartum support shouldn’t mean, “Call me if you need anything.”

It means DO SOMETHING.

Bring food.  Wash the dishes. Fold the laundry.
Take the older kids. Hold the baby between feeds. Take a nighttime shift when possible.
Protect a block of uninterrupted sleep.

Because caring for the baby without caring for the mother is not postpartum care.

We have to stop asking mothers to do it all.

A healthy baby is important.

A healthy mother matters too.

And sometimes supporting her starts with something as basic—and as medically important—as letting her sleep.

Here’s what every woman needs to know:

🧠 Brain fog is real, but it’s not a diagnosis. Changes in memory, attention, and concentration are common during the menopause transition.

🧠 Your brain notices hormonal fluctuations. Changes in estrogen during perimenopause may contribute to cognitive symptoms.

🧠 The brain you bring into menopause matters. Sleep, stress, mood, cardiovascular health, metabolic health, and your life experiences all influence cognitive function.

Fueron una segunda madre, un segundo padre, una casa a la que llegar sin avisar.

Nos conocieron antes de que pudiéramos recordarnos. Supieron qué palabra pronunciábamos mal, qué comida pedíamos siempre y cómo eran nuestros padres antes de convertirse en nuestros padres. Fueron la memoria de una familia sentada a la mesa.

Por eso, cuando mueren, no perdemos solamente a una persona. Perdemos a alguien que guardaba versiones nuestras que ya no existen en la memoria de casi nadie. Perdemos una mirada en la que todavía éramos pequeño/as. Perdemos el lugar en el que, aunque tuviéramos treinta, cuarenta o cincuenta años, todavía podíamos volver a ser nieto/as.

Y entonces la ausencia aparece donde menos la esperamos. En una silla. En una receta. En un olor. En un plato que tiene todos los ingredientes y, aun así, ya no sabe igual. Porque a veces no extrañamos solamente a quien murió. Extrañamos quiénes éramos cuando todavía estaba.» ❤️‍🩹

✍🏼 📸: Por la psicóloga y divulgadora María Paula Tripaldi

I received the first copies of the newly reissued Yes Symphonic Live album on vinyl, CD, and Blu-ray featuring my illustrations. Street date 1/23/26. I wrote the following for the liner notes:

“For the new cover art, I reimagined (or “magnified”) my original 2002 Symphonic Live cover. In this new edition, we see a prehistoric shaman summoning a Talisman’s power above a vast forest – the energy of its levitating rings opening crop circle style sinkholes in the ground. 

I also created an “alternate cover” that’s a little more intimate, depicting a man and his child watching as a Talisman’s silver rings return to sacred ground overlooking a hazy canyon. As an homage to the great album artist Aubrey “Po” Powell, who masterfully directed the Symphonic Live concert film, I chose to bring back the Hipgnosis treatment of Roger Dean’s Yes logo last seen on the covers of Going For The One and Tormato.

Elsewhere, the gatefold illustration shows four colossal Talisman monuments relaying bolts of energy to open a dimensional rift. Another illustration, “Giant Under The Sun”, is a tribute to Chris Squire, featuring a humpback whale rejoicing before a massive oceanic Talisman.

Late in the process, I decided to have some fun bridging the ancient and modern eras of interdimensional reality, so I created an archival photograph of an early 20th Century explorer’s discovery of a Talisman while it’s partially exposed by melting ice, adapting a public domain photograph by Herbert G. Ponting, circa 1911.

One final note: every composition in this sleeve was modeled, composited, or digitally hand-drawn by me, except for the aforementioned Ponting photo. None of the illustrations were created using AI. However, I used Photoshop’s generative tools to clean-up and composite some of the CG renders.

Thank you to everyone at Mercury Studios for gifting me with the rare privilege of working on this special edition of Symphonic Live, and to Jordan Berliant for initially commissioning my work back in 2001-2002. I’m especially grateful for the support of the Yes fan community.”

Details here ⬇️ Rhode Island coastal road trip! 

From dramatic ocean cliffs and historic seaside mansions to charming New England villages and hidden coastal gems, Rhode Island might be small, but it is PACKED with incredible places to explore!

If you’re planning a New England road trip, here are 7 must-visit places in coastal Rhode Island you won’t want to miss! 👇

📍 Cliff Walk, Newport – Breathtaking Atlantic Ocean views, rocky coastline, and stunning Gilded Age mansions.

📍 Thomas Dambo Trolls – Discover all 5 giant, whimsical wooden sculptures hidden throughout Rhode Island!

📍 Wickford Village – One of the most charming coastal towns in New England, filled with historic homes, cute shops, and waterfront views.

📍 Beavertail State Park, Jamestown – Rugged rocky cliffs, crashing waves, a gorgeous lighthouse and some of the most beautiful coastal scenery in Rhode Island.

📍 Newport, Rhode Island – A quintessential New England seaside destination with historic streets, beautiful harbors, and incredible architecture. Bowen’s Wharf is a must do!

📍 Fort Wetherill State Park – An abandoned coastal military fort with graffiti-covered tunnels, dramatic cliffs, and amazing ocean overlooks.

📍 The Breakers Mansion – Step inside one of America’s most spectacular Gilded Age mansions!

Whether you’re visiting Rhode Island for a weekend getaway, exploring Newport and Jamestown, or planning an epic New England fall road trip, these are some of the best places to add to your itinerary!

I never dreamed about being an actor, let alone an Executive Producer on a Hollywood movie. Not because I didn’t want to… but because my dreams only reached as far as my reality allowed them to.

My parents brought me here for a better life, and growing up, movies and television became an escape for me. They let my imagination go places my reality couldn’t.

I was that kid glued to El Pasito Tun-Tun, Tres Mujeres y un Camino, wrestling, Spider-Man, anything Disney… all on our little Zenith TV you know, the one you had to smack on the side every once in a while just to get a clear picture. 😂 That TV transported me into completely different worlds.

And now, if you squint your eyes somewhere in that frame, you’ll see my name… with Executive Producer right before it.

Like the young fellas from chicostoxico say:

“We can do it too.”

And if you made it this far down, I want you to know…

YOU CAN DO IT TOO.

Gracias, Jefecito y Jefecita. ❤️ And to everyone in my inner circle.. you all have a hand in this. In an AladinoTV interview, “Village Halloween Ritual” artistic and producing director Jeanne Fleming discussed this year’s theme, “Body & Soul,” as an invitation to step away from screens and be more present with one another.

The theme reflects a concern that so much of modern life happens through devices and virtual selves. Fleming’s message for parade night is to return to the physical world: move, dance, share the music, and connect even with people you have just met. The goal is more than a spectacle; it is a reminder that creativity and community can make everyday life feel more human.

The parade’s official theme description similarly calls on New Yorkers to reconnect body and spirit through imagination and dance. For one night, the avenue becomes a place to put phones aside, join the crowd, and experience the city together.

[{'caption': 'Le café devient une expérience technologique

Dans certaines grandes villes, commander un café ne consiste plus seulement à choisir entre un latte et un espresso. Des applications permettent de personnaliser chaque détail, les machines mémorisent les préférences des clients et certains établissements utilisent déjà des systèmes automatisés pour préparer les commandes les plus demandées.

Ce changement transforme aussi le café en terrain de jeu pour les marques. Design des gobelets, abonnements, fidélité numérique et éditions limitées créent une vraie culture autour d’une boisson quotidienne. Les gens ne paient plus uniquement pour la caféine : ils achètent un lieu, une ambiance et parfois même une petite part de leur identité en ligne.', 'datetime': '2026-10-21T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4012696656905361783', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-lax7-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/855061100_17984667504088867_1897838958716768021_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=105&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiRkVFRC5iZXN0X2ltYWdlX3VybGdlbi5DMyJ9&_nc_ohc=FlnJ2izozQEQ7kNvwHX6M1i&_nc_oc=AdoS8bmFyjNNrbnWCapaLSez0ItuqwxNFXHLGBt3Tf7UTZAcvfygYvHDaSOtQALbmWg&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-lax7-1.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=EfLCH8Mm0paksSQqvEcbkA&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQSY3I9rHZTtkxbFCRtEiHrdwW9K8chhjqBLvuhCCRU63w&oe=6AED570F', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Image', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/Dev9llqPdl3'}, {'caption': 'Parecen dos formas de comprar un reloj, pero no ofrecen la misma relación con el tiempo.

Un reloj mecánico funciona con energía almacenada en un muelle principal. Sus engranajes, escape y volante regulan el movimiento sin depender de una batería. Puede ser automático, cargándose con el movimiento de la muñeca, o manual, mediante la corona.

Un reloj de cuarzo usa una pequeña batería y un cristal de cuarzo que vibra a una frecuencia muy estable cuando recibe electricidad. Esas vibraciones controlan el avance de las agujas o de la pantalla con gran precisión.

¿Por qué importa? Mesmo com consoles cada vez mais realistas, jogos de tabuleiro modernos estão vivendo uma nova fase. Estratégia, mistério e competição presencial viraram conteúdo para criadores, cafés temáticos e noites entre amigos. Muitos títulos também usam aplicativos para controlar trilhas sonoras, missões secretas e partidas mais dinâmicas.

O mais curioso é que as empresas não estão vendendo apenas uma caixa com peças: estão criando experiências. Edições de colecionador, miniaturas detalhadas e expansões limitadas transformam alguns jogos em itens desejados por fãs e colecionadores. Durante años, los vuelos baratos hicieron que viajar de noche en tren pareciera una idea del pasado. Ahora, varias rutas europeas están recuperando vagones cama modernos, cenas a bordo y compartimentos privados para viajeros que prefieren convertir el trayecto en parte de la experiencia.

La tendencia encaja con una nueva forma de viajar: menos prisas, menos tiempo perdido en aeropuertos y más interés por recorridos con vistas. Para hoteles, operadores turísticos y marcas de lujo, el tren nocturno también abre un mercado interesante. Dormirse en una ciudad y despertarse en otra ya no suena antiguo; para muchos viajeros, empieza a sentirse como el plan más exclusivo del viaje.', 'datetime': '2026-10-19T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4011879301627462979', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-lax3-2.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/850614795_17984490858088867_5368970744486885134_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=106&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiRkVFRC5iZXN0X2ltYWdlX3VybGdlbi5DMyJ9&_nc_ohc=0a0Jb8D5MN0Q7kNvwHZXvI5&_nc_oc=AdpQIehiimo1n6j7_8FoD3soTlBqmaAQzC1oZKU7eJCG5N1qQybwufPxDgkDOTTmd-8&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-lax3-2.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=EfLCH8Mm0paksSQqvEcbkA&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQQsXaVLSjPVNg18MuAuUufTRx3Xj5ZX0uA1JlExunLZ-Q&oe=6AED5132', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Image', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/DetDvgPP0VD'}, {'caption': 'Tres pistas de que el césped no tiene dos tonos distintos.

Una franja del campo parece verde oscuro desde la grada.

La siguiente se ve mucho más clara, aunque ambas tienen la misma altura.

Cuando cambia el ángulo de la cámara, algunas franjas parecen intercambiar sus colores.

La diferencia no suele estar en el tipo de hierba, sino en su dirección. Al cortar el césped en pasadas alternas, las cuchillas doblan las hojas hacia lados opuestos. Las hojas inclinadas hacia ti reflejan más luz y se ven claras; las que apuntan en sentido contrario reflejan menos y parecen oscuras. Es el mismo efecto que hace que la tela de terciopelo cambie de tono al pasar la mano. Un patrón deportivo muy visible creado por luz, ángulo y miles de hojas diminutas.', 'datetime': '2026-10-19T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '4011748144810252475', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-lax3-2.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/856515430_17984458926088867_2226827394753736562_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=100&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiRkVFRC5iZXN0X2ltYWdlX3VybGdlbi5DMyJ9&_nc_ohc=F8mkxLQqF0oQ7kNvwHuOMpa&_nc_oc=Adof2W44DE5h-bZ7WtteczN6wSbNEbxWwf7rI41EnvKwibMX1Us6kZtbrWKYea2ga_w&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-lax3-2.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=EfLCH8Mm0paksSQqvEcbkA&_nc_ss=7a689&oh=00_AQQNu1DGrZNZ7z5gk7ANGu3RfQYgtl1ZrdFgCJfp6LKWig&oe=6AED40BC', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Image', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/Desl667v1i7'}, {'caption': 'Le tourisme spatial devient une vraie vitrine du luxe

Pendant longtemps, aller dans l’espace ressemblait à un rêve réservé aux astronautes. Aujourd’hui, plusieurs entreprises vendent déjà des expériences de vol suborbital à des clients prêts à payer très cher pour quelques minutes en apesanteur et une vue de la Terre depuis les limites de l’espace.

AI systems need enormous computing power. That means data centers need more than advanced chips. They also need reliable electricity, cooling, high-speed fiber networks and connections to the power grid.

The challenge is that AI infrastructure can expand quickly, while building new power plants, transmission lines and grid connections can take years.

U.S. data centers used an estimated 177–192 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2024. One industry estimate suggests demand could reach 383–793 TWh by 2030, depending on how quickly AI and other data-center workloads grow.

That is a huge range, but the direction highlights an important economic question: can electricity infrastructure keep pace with the AI boom?

The bigger lesson is that the future of AI depends on geography as much as technology. Places with reliable power, strong grids, fiber connections and room to expand may gain a major competitive advantage.

From 1939 to 1950, Shenandoah National Park gave us one corner of the mountain: Lewis Mountain, at mile 57.5 on Skyline Drive. Forty picnic tables, thirty campsites and one bathroom. Our voices. Our style. Our names. Our energy. Too loud. Too much. Too Black.

Black people have been taught to shrink to survive, and the research shows what it’s costing us. 👇🏾

🧠 Our minds: Code-switching means changing how we talk, look and act to make others comfortable. Studies of Black professionals link it to constant vigilance and burnout.

💼 Our livelihoods: Nearly 4 in 10 Black workers who code-switch say their careers would suffer if they stopped.

🩺 Our bodies: Researchers call it “weathering”: the constant stress of racism wears the body down and opens the door to high blood pressure, diabetes and early disease. One study found Black women in midlife were biologically 7.5 years “older” than white women the same age.

😊 Our joy: On the other side, people who get to be authentic report greater well-being and less depression over time.

So let me say it plainly: being yourself is not a luxury. It’s a health issue.

That’s why TRUTHING became my mission: to create spaces where people feel safe being exactly who they are. No mask. No shrinking. No apologies.

Walk in your truth. Your body, your mind and your joy depend on it.

[{'caption': 'Ever looked under a rock and found a whole neighborhood? 🐚

That's what our STEM Excursions Camp kids do at the tide pools. Sea stars, anemones, hermit crabs, all living side by side in one small pool of seawater that gets hot at noon and cold at midnight, dry at low tide and splashed at high tide.

Screen time is one flat world. A tide pool is thousands of living things solving survival problems in six inches of water, and kids can touch it, count it, and argue about it with their friends.

Real science our campers practice out there:
🧪 Counting species in one pool, then comparing pools. That's biodiversity data.
🌊 Watching how each creature holds on when the waves hit. That's physical adaptation.
☀️ Noticing shells close at low tide and open underwater. That's cause and effect.

Ask your kid on the way home: "If you lived in a tide pool, what would you need to survive a wave?" You'll get answers no worksheet ever produced.

We keep it screen-free on purpose. Curiosity doesn't need a charger.

Learn more about our camps and school programs at brainiacsadventures.com

This week's Game of the Week is Memory Match, and the life skill is MEMORY and FOCUS.

Here's how it works: every card starts face down. On your turn, you flip two. If they match, you keep the pair. If they don't, they turn back over, and that's where the real game begins. Players who pay attention to every single flip, even on someone else's turn, build a mental map of the whole table.

While they play, children practise:

🧠 Memory: holding a growing picture of the board in their mind.
👁️ Focus and attention: noticing every card that gets revealed, not just their own.
🔄 Working memory: connecting "the whale was over there" to their next move.
🌱 Resilience: staying patient when a pair slips away and trying again.

It's also one of the few games where a quiet observer can beat a busy player, a gentle lesson in how paying attention is itself a skill.

Memory Match is one of the 120+ games in the Brainiacs Adventures library. We use purposeful, screen-free play in our school programs and camps for children ages 5 to 13.

WEEKEND TIP: THE HOMEMADE PAIRS GAME

Draw or print 8 to 10 matching pairs with your child (animals, snacks, family faces), shuffle, and lay them face down. Play a round together, then ask: "What have you seen so far?" Hearing them explain what they remember is the real win.

What's the first pair your child always seems to find, no matter how well you shuffle? Tell us below! 👇

FIVE FOLDS. HOW MANY LAYERS? 🧠📄

The Folding Staircase is today's Brain Teaser Wednesday puzzle, and it's one your family can solve with something already in the kitchen drawer.

Ava has one big sheet of paper. She folds it in half. Then in half again. Then in half again, keeping every fold lined up neatly, never unfolding.

Every single fold doubles the number of layers.

Here's the challenge:
After 5 folds, how many layers is Ava holding?

BONUS STUMPER (for the brave): Ava keeps folding. Which fold number is the FIRST one to give her more than 100 layers? Guess before you calculate, doubling is sneaky. 😉

Hint: Start small. Write down how many layers after 1 fold, then 2 folds, then 3. The staircase builds itself.

No screens needed for this one, just paper, hands, and a family huddle. Comment your answers before peeking below! And tag the family member who always takes guesses to the next level.

━━━━━━━━━━━━ SPOILER, STOP HERE IF YOU'RE STILL SOLVING ━━━━━━━━━━━━

The answers:
Fold 1 = 2 layers
Fold 2 = 4 layers
Fold 3 = 8 layers
Fold 4 = 16 layers
Fold 5 = 32 layers ✅

For the bonus: fold 6 = 64 layers, and fold 7 = 128 layers, so the 7th fold is the first one to break past 100. Most families guess 10 or 11 folds. Doubling moves faster than anyone expects!

Try it for real: fold a sheet of paper and count the layers at each step. Around 6 or 7 folds it gets famously hard to fold any further, and your kids will love discovering why.

This screen-free puzzle builds number sense, pattern recognition, prediction, and a first feel for exponential growth, the same kind of thinking families practice through brain teasers and our 120+ board games at Brainiacs Adventures.

You’ll need: a plastic bottle, white vinegar, baking soda, a balloon, and a spoon. A funnel helps, too.

1️⃣ Half-fill the bottle with vinegar.
2️⃣ Spoon 2–3 spoonfuls of baking soda into the empty balloon.
3️⃣ Stretch the balloon over the bottle opening without letting the baking soda fall in.
4️⃣ Lift the balloon and watch the baking soda drop. What happens?

The baking soda and vinegar react and produce carbon dioxide gas. The gas takes up space and fills the balloon. 🥶 Increased opportunities for Arctic air intrusions
🌨️ A more favorable background pattern for winter weather—if moisture and the storm track cooperate

My forecast favors below-average snowfall across most of New England.

This is not a snowless-winter forecast. I expect storms and several meaningful snow opportunities. I’m questioning how often those storms will have enough cold air to remain snow from beginning to end.

WHY BELOW AVERAGE?

• NOAA expects a strong-to-very strong El Niño through January–March 2027.

• CPC favors a warmer winter across much of the interior Northeast while also showing a wetter Eastern Seaboard. Wet does not automatically mean snowy. Cold air may be the limiting factor.

• A westerly QBO combined with El Niño generally favors a stronger, more stable polar vortex. That can reduce prolonged negative-AO cold outbreaks.

• The PDO remains negative, so previous strong El Niño winters are not perfect comparisons.

• The NAO and AO cannot be predicted for the entire winter. One blocked stretch could still produce a major nor’easter and quickly change seasonal totals.

When I think about the Halloween storm of 1991, I think about the families waiting for a boat that would never come home.

Thirteen people died, including all six men aboard the Andrea Gail. Behind the famous book and movie are families who have carried that loss for 35 years. ❤️

The meteorology was extraordinary:

🌬️ Cold Canadian air helped strengthen a low near Nova Scotia.
🌀 Hurricane Grace supplied tropical moisture and energy.
🛑 Powerful high pressure blocked the storm and helped drive relentless winds across the Atlantic.

The storm moved westward toward New England. Some coastal locations faced waves around 25 feet high, with storm surge 4–5 feet above normal tides. The pounding continued through multiple high tides.

Along Maine’s coast, homes flooded, beaches eroded and coastal structures suffered extensive damage. Even President George H.W. Bush’s home in Kennebunkport was badly damaged. Across the affected coastline, boats sank and thousands of lobster traps were destroyed. Total storm damage exceeded $200 million in 1991 dollars.

As a meteorologist with Maine close to my heart, this storm hits hard. Every marine forecast reaches people trying to make a living—and families hoping they make it home.

Remembering those lost, everyone who endured it, and the rescuers who answered the call.

What do you remember about the storm of 1991?

Homemade meat sauce, sautéed onions, fresh garlic and basil, and layers of melted mozzarella and Pecorino Romano. Saucy, cheesy, and worth grabbing seconds. 🤤

SAVE THIS RECIPE 👇
Serves 8–10 | Deep 9×13-inch dish | 375°F

🛒 INGREDIENTS

• 1 lb ground beef
• 1 lb mild Italian sausage, casings removed
• 1 tbsp olive oil
• 1 large onion, diced
• 6 garlic cloves, minced
• 2 tbsp tomato paste
• 2 cans crushed tomatoes, 28 oz each
• 1 cup water, plus more as needed
• 1 tsp dried oregano
• ½ cup chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving
• Salt and black pepper, to taste
• About 9 oz oven-ready/no-boil lasagna noodles
• 24 oz shredded low-moisture mozzarella
• 1 cup grated Pecorino Romano

👨‍🍳 MAKE IT

1️⃣ Sauté the onion in olive oil over medium heat for 6–8 minutes. Add beef and sausage; cook until fully browned. Drain excess grease. Stir in garlic for 30 seconds, then tomato paste for another minute.

2️⃣ Add crushed tomatoes, water, and oregano. Simmer gently for 20–25 minutes. Stir in basil and season to taste. Keep the sauce loose and spoonable—add a splash of water if it thickens.

3️⃣ Lightly oil a deep 9×13-inch dish. Spread 1 cup sauce across the bottom. Layer dry noodles, meat sauce, mozzarella, and pecorino. Repeat for 3–4 noodle layers, finishing with sauce and cheese. Every noodle, including the edges, needs sauce covering it!

4️⃣ Cover tightly with foil, lightly oiling the underside so the cheese doesn’t stick. Set on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake at 375°F for 45–50 minutes. Check the noodles with a knife; if still firm, keep covered and bake another 10 minutes before checking again. Once tender, uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden.

5️⃣ Rest 15 minutes. Finish with fresh basil, scoop out a generous portion, and grab some garlic bread for that extra sauce. 😋

The words in this clip came from his final rule, where he spoke about imperfection, grace, and his Christian faith. 

Pratt's message challenges the idea that self-acceptance means believing you are already perfect. His perspective is that being imperfect is part of being human, and accepting that reality can make room for grace—the understanding that we don't have to earn our worth by becoming flawless. For Pratt, that grace is rooted in his Christian faith and the sacrifice of Jesus Christ. Whether you share that faith or not, the broader idea is worth reflecting on: you don't have to be perfect to be worthy of love, growth, or forgiveness. Accepting your imperfections doesn't mean giving up on becoming better; it means becoming better without believing you must first become perfect.

[{'caption': 'Ever since I first saw the cast of @tdwpmovie 2, I knew @simoneashley would make me feel the most represented. And they absolutely nailed it! 🥹🤎🖤

Growing up in a middle class, “Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, Teacher” household in New Delhi, dreaming about working in Fashion was a distant dream. 

One part of the struggle was assuring your family that this is a stable career choice and the other meant fitting in. 

Seeing very less desi/brown representation in Fashion growing up didn’t help much either. The alternatives available in Bollywood, definitely painted a realistic picture but wasn’t enough to convince the parents.

Years later, having worked numerous Assistant jobs in Fashion in London, having lived the “dream”, it still felt quite challenging because I was often the only brown/desi girl on the team.

It’s 2026 and we’re finally making the move of representing brown girls working in Fashion. With @bhavithamandava becoming the face of @chanelofficial and @bhoomikayadav27 getting casted in major shows and runways, I think it’s finally time that brown/desi girls like me are being seen working in the industry. 🤎🖤

We worked on the design of advanced spacesuits—a cool, really complicated challenge that requires applying a lot of math and science knowledge.

It was hard. It required collaboration with a range of experts—and it required asking a lot of questions. It was impossible to make progress without talking about what I didn’t get.

Talking openly about things I didn’t understand? That was hard, too.

Growing up, I’d been part of an educational system—so many of us are—that rewarded me for providing back other people’s explanations. I got pretty good at doing that. When I could do that, and yet also feel like I didn’t actually grasp the essence of something, I didn’t know how to deal with that second part. So, sometimes I really struggled to apply knowledge because I hadn’t talked about what aspects of it didn’t make sense, hadn’t talked about the challenge I was having applying it to a physical system I was trying to design.

But at MIT, as part of a research group with this amazing professor named Dava Newman, I realized the power of interactive sense-making for deep learning. In this throwback episode, I sat down with Garrett White on To My Sons and Daughters and we talked about the years of continuous movement that marked his early career. Between 2000 and 2009 he built companies in banking and insurance as a young entrepreneur, driven by the belief that life’s purpose was constant expansion and the ongoing discovery of who he was. That drive produced real results.

His largest realization over the past two years was that no external marker: location, car, house, experience, wire transfer, or closed deal has ever fully satisfied the inner desire. The premise that the next expansion would finally settle the restlessness proved false.

That is the part I want my sons and daughters to carry. Do not build an identity that depends on the next achievement to feel complete. The drive to grow can be good, yet the refusal to examine the discontent underneath it turns every success into temporary relief rather than lasting ground. (even if you have already submitted a claim)

Long story short… The PACT Act was a law signed by Biden on 8/10/22 and is viewed as the most significant expansion of VA benefits in decades. It’s short for Sergeant First Class (SFC) Health Robinson Honoring Our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act of 2022. 

It provides new and expanded benefits for Vets (and their survivors) exposed to burn pits and other toxic substances. Benefits of the PACT Act include: 
- Expanded access to VA health care 
- New and expanded presumptive conditions
- Increased compensation for service-connected disabilities
- New and expanded benefits for survivors. 

The VA offers a simple and easy to read visual to understand which route to apply is best for you (or your loved one). Check our link in bio to access this doc!

If you, or a veteran, family member, or survivor would like more information about the PACT Act and your VA Benefits, start with one of these options: 
- Visit the online portal, create an account and ask questions: ask.VA.gov 
- Call for 24/7/365 help: 1-800-MyVA411 
- Walk-In to your local care provider: VA.gov/find/locations 
- Ask your local VA org for help (VA.gov/disability/get-help-filing-claim) 
Check the New Health Care & Benefits Map provided by the VA: https://www.va.gov/files/2023-02/Journey%20Map_Accessing%20VA%20Benefits%2C%20Services%20V2.28.2023%201530hrs_2.pdf
(Link in bio!)

Have you or a loved one applied yet? What’s holding you back? We want to hear what you think. Hit us up in our DM or let’s talk about it in the comments…

- The process can take months or years. The sooner you start, the sooner you will receive your benefits.
- You may lose your backpay if you delay. The VA pays backpay to vets from the date of their injury or illness to the date their claim is approved. 
- Your medical records may become more difficult to obtain. 
- Your condition may worsen over time. This could make it more difficult to prove your disability.

#2 - Prepare your documentation
Don't skip getting a medical opinion, it can help strengthen your case
- Make a copy of your DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty)
- Collect all relevant medical records, both military and civilian
- Gather a statement from a medical professional or other expert attesting to the nature and severity of your disability (Don’t forget about mental health claims if needed, your brain health matters too)

#3 - Common Mistakes and how to avoid them
Mistakes
- Incomplete, insufficient and/or incorrect docs
- Missing deadlines 
- Lack of medical evidence
- Quitting after your claim is denied

How to avoid them
- Incomplete, insufficient and/or incorrect docs
- Missing deadlines 
- Lack of medical evidence
- Quitting after your claim is denied

#4 - Seek professional assistance
Services
- Helping you to understand which benefits you are eligible for
- Helping you gather and organize your evidence
- Reviewing your claim form and providing feedback
- Representing you before the VA during the claims process
- Appealing a denied claim

Benefits
- Increase chances of success
- Reduced stress 
- More time for you to focus on your health and well-being

#5 - Dealing with denials 
- File a Notice of Disagreement (NOD): An NOD is a formal request to the VA to review its decision. 
- Request a Decision Review Officer (DRO) review: A DRO is a VA employee who reviews denied claims and makes recommendations on whether to approve or deny them. 
- Appeal to the Board of Veterans Appeals (BVA): The BVA is a panel of three judges who review denied claims. 
- File a new claim: If you have new evidence, you can file a new claim

The 17-year-old was knocked straight to the ground when a firework suddenly exploded as he reached for it.

He had been with friends at a local park after leaving an organised display when someone lit a firework that failed to go off.

The teenager made the split-second decision to go over and try to relight it.

By the time his mum Julie received a panicked phone call from his friends and rushed to the scene, her son was already in the back of an ambulance.

She said: "I didn't take my eyes off him, I was devastated. I had to watch as his eye leaked down the side of his face."

He was rushed to James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough where consultants confirmed he had permanently lost his left eye and part of his eyelid.

The blast also left him with minor burns to his arm and leg and a broken front tooth.

Specialist surgeons had to remove fragments of firework residue from his eye socket before inserting a ball-shaped prosthesis to replicate the movement of a real eye.

[{'caption': 'I asked men and women the exact same question:

“If you were guaranteed safety after dark, what would you do?”

Some of the men didn’t even understand the question.

The women did.

“I’d go for a walk.”
“I’d sit alone on a park bench.”
“I’d go dancing.”
“I’d just… be outside.”

Nothing extraordinary.

That’s what struck me most.

Women weren’t asking for adventure.
They were asking for the freedom to do ordinary things without calculating the risk.

For so many men, nighttime simply means the day got darker.

Prop 1 could open the state Constitution to a broad rewrite. Prop 2 targets political money from utilities and major government contractors.
Here’s what you need to know before November.

Proposal 1 asks Michigan voters whether they want to call a Constitutional Convention, commonly called a Con-Con, to undertake a general revision of the Michigan Constitution. This question automatically appears on the ballot every 16 years, and Michigan voters have repeatedly declined to call a convention, including in 1978, 1994 and 2010.

And this is not a proposal to fix one outdated sentence or make one narrowly defined change.

A “general revision” means opening Michigan’s foundational governing document to potentially sweeping changes. A convention could revisit provisions dealing with voting and elections, reproductive freedom, civil rights, taxation, property rights, public pensions, collective bargaining, the powers of state government and much more.

That is what makes Proposal 1 so consequential.

Proposal 2 targets a familiar problem in Michigan politics: companies that depend on decisions from state government can also spend money influencing the people making those decisions.

The proposal would restrict certain political contributions from regulated electric and gas utilities, including DTE and Consumers Energy, as well as companies receiving more than $250,000 a year in government contracts. The restrictions would also reach certain executives, board members and others closely connected to those companies.

The argument from supporters is simple: the companies being regulated shouldn’t be financially supporting the politicians responsible for regulating them.

That concern is especially relevant with Michigan’s monopoly utilities, which rely on state regulators for major decisions involving rates and investments while remaining deeply involved in state politics.

[{'caption': "We have some amazing news to share! 

We're over the moon to have been awarded £192,855 from The National Lottery Heritage Fund to celebrate our incredible heritage and future proof the Rio for years to come.\xa0

As we mark 50 years of being run by and for the community, this grant will support community archiving sessions and a wide-ranging consultation with the many audiences we serve in Hackney. The Rio's heritage is held in our iconic Grade 2 listed cinema building and also held by the people of Hackney so we will be collecting your memories, your stories and also your hopes for the future of the Rio

This will be a year-long project, and the grant will also fund:
* A condition survey of our building
* Work on improving accessibility
* A sustainability audit
* Legal support
* Architectural work to plan a refurbishment
* Business planning
* Fundraising

We'll also be working on a documentary about the Rio and it's place in the community!\xa0

A huge thank you to National Lottery players for making this possible, and to the Culture and Heritage teams (@Love.Hackney) and Hackney Archives (@ArchivesHackney) for their invaluable advice and ongoing support of the Rio. Thanks also to Film London (@film_london) and our patrons Asif Kapadia (@asifkapadia1), Sally Potter (@sallypotter) and Dionne Edwards (@dionce_knowledge).

Love and thanks to the community of Rio staff, trustees, regular programmers and audiences who keep the dream alive.\xa0

We can’t wait to share more about how you can get involved over the next year! Stay tuned for how you can take part in our community archiving days - sign up to our newsletter!\xa0

Eddie, AKA Eddie Baroo, Ed, Eddie Baby, Eduardo, Edmont, Edison, Baby, Bear, Baby Bear, Triple B (BaBy Bear), The Prince, and The Prince of Pawtucket, bravely crossed the rainbow bridge on Wednesday morning, while his parents held his paws as he found peace. He had just celebrated his 10th birthday on May 18. Although he my have been older than we thought, as a rescue, his birthday was not certain, and we thought we had years left. As it turned out, God needed another angel that day. Eddie passed away after a sudden and unanticipated medical event that ripped him from us in a matter of hours. There were no warning signs. The vets believe it was an undetected brain tumor or stroke. Had he become stable after arresting, his prognosis was extremely unfavorable, and any time left would have likely meant severe mental and physical deficits. Now that you know the horrible part, it’s only fair the rest of his story is told. 

Prior to coming to Rhode Island, Eddie was living in the Ozarks in northern Arkansas for the first two years of his life. Veterinary staff believe he was hit by a car when he was found in 2018. Eddie showed his resiliency and recovered with a slightly wonky walk if you looked closely enough. He was brought into the hands of Save One Soul Animal Rescue League, who brought him to Rhode Island in May 2018. 

At the age of two, Eddie was already a star. He was the featured adoptable dog that SOSARL showed off at a Pawtucket Red Sox game at McCoy Stadium, unbeknownst to his mom, who lived just five minutes away. It wasn’t until an adoption day on June 2, 2018 that Eddie ran into the lap and heart of his new mom, with his grandmom nearby who affirmed he chose her.

A wider geopolitical reading of Sachs’ remarks reflects the broader debate over the transition from a US-led international system towards a more contested and multipolar order.

His comments highlight the risks of misreading shifts in power, particularly as major states compete to shape the future of global governance, security and economic influence.

And honestly, I think this is where a lot of the money conversation gets too shallow.

Yes, personal responsibility matters. Budgeting matters. Avoiding dumb debt matters. Learning to say no matters. Nobody is helped by pretending our choices don’t matter at all.

But we also have to be honest about the math.

For a lot of households, the biggest problem is not that they bought too many coffees. It is that rent, groceries, insurance, cars, medical bills, utilities, and everything else decided to show up to the same party at the same time.

And then the advice they get is often from someone who bought a house when prices, interest rates, wages, insurance, and the entire cost structure looked completely different.

That does not mean older generations had it easy. They had their own pressures, sacrifices, and struggles. Every generation has had to figure out how to survive the economy they were handed.

But it does mean we should be careful about giving 1995 advice to someone living with 2026 prices.

The answer is not to give up. The answer is also not to pretend this is all fixed by canceling Netflix.

The real answer is more complicated.

Spend wisely. Build skills. Increase income when you can. Avoid lifestyle creep. Don’t finance every want. Be patient. Make boring decisions that compound over time.

[{'caption': 'Our book is here!!

It’s an amazing feeling of recognition, I have to tell you, in a year of what had felt like a hopeless, uphill battle against bot accounts in the thousands stealing my studio’s work. Many of these accounts take subscriptions posing as me. People have reached out telling me they’ve been donating for months only to realize the fake accounts were not the original artist - us. 

Many of them just sell books, or resell our videos as “viral” packages. It’s been a crash course in emotional and mental strength trying to contend with the age of the internet in such a massive way. So having the recognition of my beautiful team at Penguin feels like such a victory. Moreso, having so many of you share such heartfelt and genuine stories with me about your lives because of the book, is even more impacting. Thank you for your recognition. 

The book, despite all the chicanery of thieves, has been a wild success in every inconceivable way. Thank you!!!! 
It’s releasing in just a few days in Australia too and I cannot wait to see it around my little Tasman island! 

Love to y’all!!

For the past four years I have dedicated my life nearly entirely to animation and the understanding of directing stories. Simultaneously I have tried, with what little free time I could muster, to make money, that necessary thing so needed for food, rent and running a business. 

As I have set my sights on film-making, my job has been less that of an animator, and that of a writer and director, storyboarding the things I want to share with the world. 

When studio Ghibli produced its first film, Nausicaä, (actually this was technically not produced by Ghibli but tomato-tomato) it cost around 1 million dollars. To do the same thing today would be roughly 40 million dollars. In design we look at the 2 of 3 rule: 

You can choose 2 of the following. 

GOOD - FAST - CHEAP. 

Good and cheap won’t be fast. 
Good and fast won’t be cheap. 
Fast and cheap won’t be good. 

There is always a sacrifice, and now moreso the doubt creeps in, because the stakes are higher, and they will be higher for future generations as well. I’m 34. I don’t have a massive team, I don’t have a financier, and in the world of AI, it’s quite difficult convincing anyone the old ways are worth investing in. 

I’m sharing all of this to be honest with you, not just to share my achievements of which I believe I have many, but to convey a bit of the authentic process behind what’s currently going on in my head. I want to make a movie, I believe I have a story to tell that’s worth telling.

My team of 7 is quite small, and we are stretched then, and it is costly. To achieve a 2D movie in the modern era, would require probably another 50 employees (some modern techniques have made production less strenuous) 

A film is coming, it’s going to happen if my time here on earth allows it. And it will have the visuals so often loss in modern day cinema. I am so thankful for all of you being here who have supported us every step of the way. 

I have seen countless stories become shelved, bought out, shut up, shut down, and started but never finished for any number of reasons. I’ll do this even if it’s just myself, even if it takes years. ​This intense exchange cuts to the core of modern American politics and the ongoing battle between the executive branch and the federal judiciary. For years, debates over whether unelected district judges should possess the authority to halt federal policies nationwide have deeply divided Republicans and Democrats. Conservatives like Hawley argue that weaponized nationwide injunctions severely obstruct duly elected executive agendas, while pointing out partisan shifts in how legal scholars defend or condemn these judicial interventions depending on who occupies the White House.

​The clip highlights the broader Republican push to rein in judicial overreach and restore constitutional boundaries to the courts. As debates over executive power, judicial activism, and the rule of law continue to dominate Washington, exchanges like this underline the deep institutional friction defining contemporary U.S. governance. This year, @kaitlinh4273 and I got to sit down with her and go through EVERY proposition and candidate. And GIIIIRRLLL, she had OPINIONS! She even had me researching EVERY SINGLE JUDGE on the ballot! Lol.

Me and my grandma, two generations of Black women sitting together, discussing politics, doing our research, and exercising a right she and our ancestors fought so hard for. THAT’S LEGACY! 

And to anyone saying voting doesn’t matter, I hear you! Sometimes it really does feel that way. We vote, and we’re STILL fighting some of the same battles. But voting isn’t the only way to create change. We have to organize, hold people accountable, and keep showing up beyond Election Day.

Just because the system doesn’t always work for us doesn’t mean we stop demanding that it does!

I’m grateful to have my grandma here still teaching us the importance of using our voices and that she fought/still fights for my and YOUR right to vote. 

So do it. Go vote.

This fall, I’m opening a 6-week Grief Support Group in Austin for adults grieving the death of a spouse, parent, child, sibling, or friend. The group is also open to those grieving a divorce, estrangement, pregnancy loss, or infertility.

Each Tuesday evening focuses on a specific topic, from naming your loss to learning how to carry it forward. You’ll leave every session with practical tools grounded in established bereavement research and share the experience with a small, confidential group of people who understand what this season can hold.

The group is led by me, Roxanne Watson, a Licensed Professional Counselor and Certified Grief Informed Professional.

Tuesday evenings, November 10 to December 15, 2026
6:30 to 8p
601 Farley Drive, Austin, TX
$360 for all 6 sessions
Limited to 8 participants

To reserve your spot, email roxanne@counselingaustin.com, call 512.522.1088, or visit counselingaustin.com through the link in my bio.

⁠
Naresh Bhatt's defense attorney began by asking him about his upbringing in Nepal and the experiences that shaped his early life.⁠
⁠
He described living in a humble home built on a steep cliff with multiple families when he was a child. He said there was no heating or air conditioning in the home and they didn't have enough to eat the majority of the time.⁠
⁠
After detailing his life in Nepal, Bhatt spoke about coming to the United States and working a few odd jobs before enlisting in the Army.⁠
⁠
Bhatt said he recognized he was experiencing some mental health issues during his time in the military.⁠
⁠
"Did you start having symptoms having to do with your mental health?" his attorney asked him.⁠
⁠
"Over there? Yes. I did not realize, but, like, you know, I did not know about these, all those dreams this and that," Bhatt said.⁠
⁠
"So you're waking up screaming at night?" the attorney asked.⁠
⁠
"Yeah and then [someone asked me] 'What happened? What happened, soldier?' And then I say, like, 'nothing.' And then he found me, like, a lot of sweating and then, you know, heartbeat is going. I say, 'No, it's a bad dream. Dream is gone. Some evil bother,'" Bhatt said.⁠
⁠
After discussing Bhatt's background, his attorney eventually asked him about his relationship with Kafle.⁠
⁠
He admitted that in the months before her disappearance their relationship took a turn and that they weren't being kind to each other. But he said on the stand multiple times that he never assaulted his wife.⁠
⁠

Different countries. Different histories. Different conflicts. But civilians in all three places have endured devastating violence, displacement, hunger and humanitarian crises.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, decades of conflict, armed groups and exploitation have displaced millions. The Democratic wave extended well beyond traditional battleground states. The party flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats, including victories in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Ohio and Maine. Several of these states voted comfortably for Donald Trump in 2024, highlighting the scale of the political shift.

El-Sayed received 191,013 votes, or 91.78% of Detroit’s Senate vote. Republican Mike Rogers received 11,298 votes, or 5.43%.

El-Sayed’s share exceeded Elissa Slotkin’s 88.37% in that year’s Senate race. Rogers’ share of the city’s Senate vote fell from 7.43% in 2024.

In the campaign’s closing days, national media outlets reported concerns among Democratic supporters about El-Sayed’s campaign and outreach, while others highlighted Democrats backing Rogers.

Two days before Election Day, U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens reversed her support for El-Sayed and endorsed Rogers, appearing alongside him at Detroit’s Perfecting Church, led by Pastor Marvin L. Winans. Stevens had lost to El-Sayed in the Democratic primary.

Detroit City Council member Mary Waters told the New York Post that voters who preferred Rogers could split their tickets, but she declined to identify her own Senate choice. Her photograph also appeared in an ad promoting split-ticket voting.

[{'caption': '🚨 You can report an insurance company to your state’s Insurance Commissioner. And more people need to know this.

When an insurance company denies medically necessary care, delays payment, mishandles a claim, or engages in potentially unfair practices, you don’t have to simply accept the decision.

You can file a complaint with your state’s Insurance Commissioner — the government office responsible for regulating insurance companies and investigating certain consumer complaints.

What can happen when you file a complaint?

➡️ The insurer may be required to respond to the complaint.
➡️ The state may review whether the company followed applicable insurance laws and regulations.
➡️ The investigation may uncover a pattern of unfair practices.
➡️ Depending on the circumstances, the regulator may take further action.

⚠️ Filing a complaint does NOT guarantee that a denial will be overturned or that your claim will be paid. But it creates a formal record and gives regulators an opportunity to examine what happened.

And here’s what I want patients to understand: An insurance company’s decision is not automatically the final word on your healthcare.

Document what happened. Keep your denial letters. Save your correspondence. Understand your appeal rights. And when appropriate, file a complaint.

As a physician and an independent medical practice owner, I believe patients deserve to know that they have options when the system fails them.

Insurance companies should be held accountable to the laws that govern them.

📣 Share this with someone who has ever been told, “Your insurance won’t cover it.”

This map reveals how the familiar Mercator projection significantly distorts the size of countries, especially near the poles. Areas like Greenland, Canada, and Russia appear much larger than they truly are, while regions closer to the equator—such as Africa and South America—often look smaller than their real size.

By comparing true land areas (shown in red outlines) to their Mercator depiction (in blue), the map highlights these dramatic differences. For example, Greenland looks nearly the size of Africa on many maps, but in reality, Africa is about 14 times larger.

Understanding these distortions helps us see the world more accurately—and reminds us that maps don’t just show geography, but also influence how we perceive global importance and scale.', 'datetime': '2025-07-03T00:00:00.000Z', 'id': '3668592181282630240', 'image_url': 'https://scontent-fra3-2.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/514599809_18048454661449614_8999027398696893871_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_e35_s640x640_tt6&_nc_cat=111&ccb=7-5&_nc_sid=18de74&efg=eyJlZmdfdGFnIjoiRkVFRC5iZXN0X2ltYWdlX3VybGdlbi5DMyJ9&_nc_ohc=ZvyzLWWPwcEQ7kNvwHEoz-V&_nc_oc=AdogpDHcwjuRPp7tDDmAjlgTxTV8j5r6gb9BhLZ5hfxyLzcb2eEcy0epCb4DEF1NXcM&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent-fra3-2.cdninstagram.com&_nc_gid=aG3AjLnnXWDj_wWerS1L8Q&_nc_ss=7aa8c&oh=00_AQR40atKd1hnb01WnDOT3HJIWy7oRSPG2xu_NZ6uSx7eew&oe=6AF1987D', 'post_hashtags': None, 'content_type': 'Image', 'url': 'https://www.instagram.com/p/DLpdSbfIGpg'}, {'caption': 'How do Europeans react when you try to speak their language?

The Democratic wave extended well beyond traditional battleground states. The party flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats, including victories in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Ohio and Maine. Several of these states voted comfortably for Donald Trump in 2024, highlighting the scale of the political shift.

The result represents a major setback for President Trump halfway through his second term. Preheat the oven to 350

Add the chicken back to the skillet along with a few lemon slices and smashed cloves of garlic. Cook in the oven for about 10 minutes then brush chicken with melted butter and cook for an additional 15 to 20 minutes.

Although she became one of the most recognizable actresses in history, Marilyn faced constant pressure to fit Hollywood’s expectations. Her personal life was equally difficult. She never knew her biological father, reportedly experienced several miscarriages, and deeply wanted to have a family of her own. Accounts of her life also describe her struggles with loneliness, her search for faith, and the cruel treatment she sometimes faced, including reportedly being insulted after purchasing her own home.

Even after decades of fame, many of the struggles behind her public image remain a reminder that being adored by millions doesn’t mean someone is happy behind closed doors.

Mayors change.
Congress changes.
Political seasons change.

Pray for the people who were elected.
Pray for the people you disagree with.

Imagine a coffin remaining sealed for more than 2,500 years — then finally being opened in front of a crowd.

In October 2020, Egyptian archaeologists made headlines after opening an ancient sarcophagus at Saqqara, a historic burial site south of Cairo.

The coffin was one of 59 sealed wooden sarcophagi discovered in the area.

When the lid was lifted, researchers revealed a mummy wrapped in decorated burial linen, with colorful inscriptions still visible.

The coffins date back to Egypt’s Late Period and are believed to have belonged to priests and other prominent individuals.

The discovery offered archaeologists a remarkable glimpse into ancient Egyptian burial traditions.

More than two millennia later, the secrets of the ancient world were still being uncovered. 🏺

[{'caption': 'If Democrats had spent much of President Donald Trump’s second term searching for a way to break his grip on Washington, voters had now handed them one. The midterms generated a blue wave that swept Republicans out of power in the House and the Senate, reversing the party’s fortunes just two years after Trump’s return to the White House. The results amounted to a decisive rebuke of a President whose handling of the economy, rising prices, and the war with Iran had fueled widespread discontent, and who spent the closing days of the campaign musing about candidates’ anatomy and dismissing Americans’ concerns over their bottom line.

For the first time since Trump returned to Washington, Democrats will be able to set the legislative agenda, compel testimony from Administration officials, investigate allegations of corruption, and force Republicans to take difficult votes. Party leaders see an opportunity to turn the public’s discontent with Trump into a sustained argument for returning Democrats to the White House in 2028.

Interviews with more than two dozen Democratic leaders, strategists, and members of Congress reveal a party itching to fight on nearly every front the President has opened. But when the midterm victory laps conclude, the Democrats’ deeper problems will be waiting for them. Even leading up to their midterm victory, surveys showed the party remains unpopular. Its leaders are divided over how far left to move, what kind of economic message will win back the voters who abandoned them in 2024, and how aggressively to confront Trump.

At the link in bio, read our new cover story on how Democrats could wield their newfound power.

Take Ohio. The state has some 200 data centers, making it one of the biggest hubs in the country. In a former swing state that went red in the Trump era, Republicans admit the groundswell of political opposition to data centers has created a political opening for Democrats.

By themselves, data centers don’t rank as a top-tier national campaign issue, according to voters—in a recent survey, the economy, the future of democracy, health care, education, and immigration made up the top five. But Democratic candidates have sought to connect data centers to many of those themes.

⁠
It was one of the deadliest nights of the war for U.S. forces. But it wasn’t the only attack targeting American troops where they live and sleep. That same week, Iran hit multiple housing units at other U.S. military installations across the region.⁠
⁠
The July strikes marked an alarming shift in Iran’s tactics and revealed an improvement in the regime’s ability to sequence attacks and hit targets with precision. Iran was taking more direct aim at the buildings that house American troops, according to a Wall Street Journal analysis of satellite data, Iranian military statements and interviews with U.S. officials.⁠
⁠
In all, the Journal found 274 structures at 24 installations across the Middle East that showed damage during the war’s first six months.⁠
⁠
Iran has hit America’s installations hard. Now, with President Trump considering a new wave of attacks on Iran, the U.S. military pulled some personnel off several of those locations ahead of possible retaliation, the Journal has reported. This comes as Pentagon officials worry that the regime has conserved some of its most sophisticated missiles and could improve its attacks in the next round of fighting.⁠
⁠

⁠
The Defense Department and U.S. Central Command, which oversees military operations in the Middle East, declined to comment.⁠

How the Override Process Works

• Constitutional Rule: Under Article I, Section 7 of the U.S. Constitution, a regular veto can be overridden only by a two-thirds vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

• Chamber Sequence: The chamber where the bill originated votes first. If it fails to reach the two-thirds threshold, the bill dies and the other chamber does not vote. If it passes with two-thirds, it moves to the second chamber.

• Outcome: If both chambers achieve a two-thirds majority, the bill becomes law without the President’s signature.

• The High Bar: A two-thirds supermajority requires at least 290 votes in the House (out of 435) and 67 votes in the Senate (out of 100), meaning the opposing party must win over a significant number of members from the President’s party.

• Regular Veto: The President returns the unsigned bill with a memorandum of disapproval to the originating house of Congress within 10 days. This type can be overridden by Congress.

• Pocket Veto: If the President receives a bill and does not sign it within 10 days, and Congress has adjourned during that period—preventing the President from returning it—the bill dies. Pocket vetoes cannot be overridden because Congress is not in session to vote.
